cde.id: Have you ever used any of these drugs to feel good or high, or to feel more active or alert? Or did you use any prescription drugs when they were not prescribed, or more than prescribed?

records.idealCde: Lifetime recreational drug use history: a multi-select (checkbox) item asking which specific illicit or non-medically-used substances the respondent has EVER used in their lifetime. The question is: 'In your lifetime, which of the following substances have you ever used?' Answer type: categorical multi-select (select all that apply) from a defined list of substance categories including at minimum: marijuana/cannabis, cocaine/crack, prescription stimulants used non-medically (e.g., Ritalin, Adderall), and other common recreational/illicit substances. Each substance category is recorded as a binary indicator (yes selected / not selected). Qualifier: self-report, lifetime time window.

memberDetails.name: recreationaldruguse_whichdrugsused
memberDetails.text: In your LIFETIME, which of the following substances have you ever used?

transforms.rationale: The source variable is a multi-select 'which drugs used' checklist, while the CDE is a single yes/no/don't-know question about ever using drugs. Each specific drug selection maps to Yes (5) because selecting any drug indicates affirmative use; 'None of these drugs' maps to No (1); 'Prefer not to answer' maps to Don't know/refused (9); 'Other (Specify)' maps to Yes (5) as it implies drug use was reported. Confidence is slightly reduced because the source is a multi-select instrument and the CDE is a single binary question — the mapping is conceptually valid but the granularity differs significantly.

records.concept: Lifetime cigarette smoking status: whether smoked ≥100 cigarettes in lifetime
records.idealCde: Tobacco and nicotine product use history — a set of CDEs capturing lifetime use of combustible cigarettes and electronic nicotine delivery systems (e-cigarettes/vaping devices). Covers: (1) Lifetime cigarette smoking status: whether the individual has smoked ≥100 cigarettes (≥5 packs) in their lifetime [radio; Yes / No / Prefer not to say]; (2) Age at smoking initiation: age in whole years when the individual first started smoking cigarettes [integer, years; with upper-bound category '>60 years' and 'Prefer not to say']; (3) Total years of cigarette smoking: cumulative number of years the individual has smoked cigarettes [integer, years; with upper-bound category '>60 years' and 'Prefer not to say']; (4) Age at vaping/e-cigarette initiation: age in whole years when the individual first started vaping or using e-cigarettes [integer, years; with upper-bound category '>60 years' and 'Prefer not to say']; (5) Total years of vaping/e-cigarette use: cumulative number of years the individual has vaped or used e-cigarettes [integer, years; with upper-bound category '>20 years' and 'Prefer not to say']. All items are self-reported and pertain to the respondent's own lifetime history with no specific time-window restriction.

gencde.rationale: Derived from MESA variable cgr25 (TOTAL YEARS LIVED WITH CIGARETTE SMOKER), which is numeric. This CDE captures passive/secondhand smoke exposure duration in the household context, distinct from the individual's own smoking history (pack-years, initiation age, cessation age). The near-miss CDEs (pack-year value, start age, stop age) all pertain to active smoking by the respondent and were excluded. Unit 'a' is the UCUM code for years. Maximum of 99 reflects a practical upper bound for a human lifespan; minimum of 0 indicates no such exposure. No permissible values are defined as this is a continuous numeric field.

records.concept: Current cigarette/tobacco smoking status (do you smoke now)
records.idealCde: Tobacco use history (any type): A composite CDE capturing both current and lifetime regular tobacco use across all product types. gencde.title: Chewing Tobacco Use Status and Recency (Never/Former/Current; Used in Last 30 Days)
gencde.definition: A categorical assessment of an individual's chewing tobacco use history and recency, capturing whether the person has never used, formerly used, or currently uses chewing tobacco, with current use further qualified by whether the product was used in the preceding 30 days.
gencde.questionText: What is this person's chewing tobacco use status — have they never used, formerly used, or do they currently use chewing tobacco; and if current, did they use chewing tobacco in the last 30 days?

gencde.rationale: Two source fields from MESA were harmonized: chew1c (never/former/current) and chwcur1 (used in last 30 days, yes/no). The canonical permissible-value set merges these by nesting the 30-day recency qualifier within the 'Current' category, yielding four mutually exclusive codes. Never (0) and Former (1) are unambiguous from chew1c; Current is split into 'not in last 30 days' (2) and 'used in last 30 days' (3) using chwcur1. No answer concepts were added beyond those observed. Near-miss CDEs (Tobacco product used type; Tobacco current use indicator; Tobacco use duration) informed aliases only. Confidence is moderate (0.78) because the composite encoding of two source fields into one CDE introduces a structural assumption that chwcur1 applies exclusively to current users.

records.idealCde: Smoking cessation attempt history: a cluster of related but distinct smoking behavior constructs covering (1) serious quit attempt — whether the individual has ever made a serious attempt to quit smoking (stopped for ≥1 day with intent to quit); categorical single-select: Yes / No / Don't know / Prefer not to answer; (2) current tobacco smoking status — whether the individual currently smokes tobacco; categorical single-select: Yes on most or all days / Only occasionally / No / Prefer not to answer; (3) sustained cessation — whether the individual ever stopped smoking for more than 6 months during the period they smoked; categorical single-select: Yes / No / Do not know / Prefer not to answer; (4) likelihood of resuming smoking — whether the individual thinks they may start smoking again (asked of former smokers who had a sustained cessation episode); categorical single-select: Yes definitely / Yes probably / No probably not / No definitely not / Do not know / Prefer not to answer; (5) maternal smoking around birth — whether the participant's biological mother smoked regularly around the time of the participant's birth (a distinct environmental/exposure variable, not self-reported smoking behavior); categorical single-select: Yes / No / Do not know / Prefer not to answer. NOTE: These five fields carry different qualifiers (self-reported quit behavior, self-reported current status, self-reported sustained cessation, self-reported relapse likelihood, and maternal perinatal exposure) and should be represented as separate CDEs rather than collapsed into one.

gencde.title: Likelihood of Resuming Smoking Among Former Daily Smokers with Sustained Cessation (≥6 Months)
gencde.definition: Among individuals who previously smoked tobacco on most or all days and subsequently stopped for more than 6 months, a self-reported assessment of the perceived likelihood that they will start smoking again.
gencde.questionText: Do you think you may start smoking again?
relatedCdes: PROMIS - Smoking nicotine dependence though of never smoke again overwhelm scale
Cigarettes Smoking Frequency
Tobacco smoking status NHIS
gencde.rationale: Source field is UKBB F2936, restricted to former daily smokers who achieved sustained cessation of >6 months (gated by F1249). Missing-data sentinels (-1=Do not know, -3=Prefer not to answer) are excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per instructions; implementers should handle these as system missing or a separate administrative code. The four retained values form a balanced Likert-style likelihood scale. Near-miss CDEs (PROMIS nicotine dependence, NHIS tobacco status, cigarette frequency) address related but distinct constructs (dependence severity, current status, quantity) and were used only to inform alias terminology.

relatedCdes: Tobacco use duration
Tobacco use started age value
Tobacco product used type
gencde.rationale: Derived from a single MESA source field (chwyrs1c). The unit '(times/d).a' follows UCUM convention for times-per-day multiplied by years. No upper bound is imposed as the distribution is cohort-dependent and right-skewed; minimum is 0 (never chewed or just started). Near-miss CDEs (tobacco use duration, age started, tobacco product type) are related but capture distinct dimensions and were not merged. Confidence is slightly below 1.0 because only one source cohort field was available for validation.

records.concept: Average weekly beer consumption (12 oz. bottles/cans per week), ordinal categorical
records.idealCde: Alcohol consumption frequency by beverage type (self-reported, average week): Three parallel CDEs capturing the typical weekly quantity consumed of each standard alcoholic beverage type — (1) beer (12 oz. bottles/cans per week), (2) liquor/spirits (1.5 oz. shots or mixed-drink equivalents per week), and (3) wine (5 oz. glasses per week). Each CDE asks: 'During an average week, how many standard servings of [beer / liquor / wine] do you usually drink?' Answer type is an ordinal categorical variable representing banded weekly counts (e.g., less than 1, 1–7, 8–14, 15–21, 22–28, 29–35, 36 or more), with a 'Prefer not to say' / decline-to-answer option. Units are standard drink servings per week specific to each beverage type. The three CDEs together constitute a beverage-specific alcohol use frequency battery for self-report in an average/typical week context.

records.concept: Average weekly wine consumption (5 oz. glasses per week), ordinal categorical
records.idealCde: Alcohol consumption frequency by beverage type (self-reported, average week): Three parallel CDEs capturing the typical weekly quantity consumed of each standard alcoholic beverage type — (1) beer (12 oz. bottles/cans per week), (2) liquor/spirits (1.5 oz. shots or mixed-drink equivalents per week), and (3) wine (5 oz. glasses per week). Each CDE asks: 'During an average week, how many standard servings of [beer / liquor / wine] do you usually drink?' Answer type is an ordinal categorical variable representing banded weekly counts (e.g., less than 1, 1–7, 8–14, 15–21, 22–28, 29–35, 36 or more), with a 'Prefer not to say' / decline-to-answer option. Units are standard drink servings per week specific to each beverage type. The three CDEs together constitute a beverage-specific alcohol use frequency battery for self-report in an average/typical week context.

gencde.title: Female Heavy Episodic Drinking Frequency — 4 or More Drinks on One Occasion in Past 12 Months
gencde.definition: Self-reported frequency with which a female participant consumed four or more alcoholic drinks at a single sitting or occasion during the preceding 12 months, used as a sex-specific threshold for heavy episodic (binge) drinking.
gencde.questionText: About how often during the past 12 months would you say you had four or more drinks at the same sitting or occasion?

gencde.rationale: Single source field (CLSA ALC_FMFQ_TRM) with a well-defined 8-level ordinal frequency scale. The 4+ drinks threshold is the NIAAA/WHO sex-specific heavy episodic drinking criterion for females (vs. 5+ for males). Codes are assigned in descending frequency order (1=most frequent, 8=never) to align with AUDIT-style conventions. Near-miss CDEs use a 6+ threshold (SAMHSA) or a 5+ male threshold; these were retained only as aliases. The 'prefer not to answer' sentinel present in the ideal anchor CDE was not observed in the source field and is therefore excluded per instructions. Confidence slightly reduced from maximum because only one cohort source field was available for reconciliation.

gencde.definition: Self-reported lifetime and current alcohol consumption status of the participant, classified as never having consumed alcohol, formerly consuming alcohol but not currently, or currently consuming alcohol.
gencde.questionText: Which of the following best describes your alcohol use: have you never consumed alcohol, do you formerly drink but no longer do, or do you currently drink alcohol?
relatedCdes: Alcohol current use indicator
Do you drink alcohol regularly (every week)?

gencde.rationale: Source fields MESA:alc1c (0=NEVER|1=FORMER|2=CURRENT) provides the primary three-level categorical structure. MESA:curalc1 and MESA:curalc5 are binary (NO/YES) indicators of current use only; their YES/NO concepts map onto CURRENT vs. NEVER-or-FORMER and are fully subsumed by the three-level scheme. The canonical permissible-value set merges YES→Current and NO→Never-or-Former, preserving the richer three-level distinction from alc1c. Codes 0/1/2 follow the MESA convention. Near-miss CDEs (regular weekly drinking indicator; PROMIS alcohol scale) were used only to inform aliases and confirm non-overlap. Confidence slightly below 1.0 because the binary fields alone cannot distinguish Never from Former without the composite alc1c field.

records.concept: Typical number of drinks per week by beverage type (beer, liquor, red wine, white wine, other) on weekdays vs. weekend days in the past 12 months
records.idealCde: Alcohol consumption by beverage type and day type (weekday vs. weekend) during the past 12 months: captures the typical number of drinks consumed per week of a specific alcoholic beverage (beer, liquor, red wine, other alcohol) on weekdays or weekend days in a typical week over the prior 12-month period. Question: 'In a typical week during the past 12 months, how many drinks of [beverage type] do you drink on [weekdays / weekend days]?' Answer type: non-negative decimal (number of drinks), with separate values per beverage type (beer, liquor, red wine, other alcohol) and per day-type stratum (weekdays, weekend days); time window qualifier: past 12 months.

gencde.rationale: This CDE is a composite template covering 10 distinct strata: 5 beverage types (beer, liquor, red wine, white wine, other alcohol) × 2 day types (weekdays, weekend days). All source fields from CLSA are decimal-valued counts of standard drinks per week within the specified stratum; no categorical permissible values apply. Maximum value is left null as no upper bound was specified in source fields; minimum is 0 (non-negative). White wine weekday and weekend fields (ALC_WHWD_NB_TRM, ALC_WHWE_NB_TRM) and beer weekend and liquor weekend fields were not explicitly listed in source but are implied by the symmetric CLSA naming pattern and the ideal CDE anchor; only confirmed source fields are cited. Near-miss CDEs address monthly or 30-day average drinks rather than the weekly by-beverage-type by-day-type structure captured here.

transforms.rationale: Source is drinks per weekday (a typical weekday), target is drinks per week on weekdays. There are 5 weekdays, so multiplying by 5 converts weekday daily drinks to weekday weekly drinks. However, the target CDE combines multiple alcohol types and both weekday/weekend, so there's ambiguity about whether the target is specifically beer on weekdays or a combined total. (llm_confidence 0.70)

Source is drinks of liquor per weekday; target appears to be drinks per week on weekdays. Multiplying by 5 (weekdays in a week) converts daily weekday consumption to weekly weekday consumption. However, the target CDE seems to aggregate all alcohol types and both weekday/weekend, which would make a simple formula insufficient. If the target is specifically liquor on weekdays in drinks/week, then source * 5 is correct. (llm_confidence 0.70)

The source asks for drinks per weekday (a daily rate for weekdays), while the target asks for drinks per week on weekdays. Multiplying by 5 (number of weekdays) converts daily weekday consumption to weekly weekday consumption. However, there is some ambiguity about whether 'source' is already a per-day or per-week figure. (llm_confidence 0.70)

records.concept: Change in alcohol intake compared to 10 years previously
records.idealCde: Alcohol and hot beverage consumption behavior: a cluster of self-reported categorical items capturing multiple distinct dimensions of drinking behavior, including (1) change in alcohol intake compared to 10 years previously (more/same/less/don't know), (2) whether alcohol is typically consumed with meals (yes/no/varies), (3) former alcohol drinker status among current non-drinkers (yes/no), (4) preferred temperature of hot drinks such as coffee or tea (very hot/hot/warm/does not drink hot drinks), and (5) reason for reducing alcohol consumption among current drinkers who drink less than 10 years ago (illness, doctor's advice, health precaution, etc.). Each dimension is a separate single-select categorical variable with response options including 'Prefer not to answer' and, where applicable, 'Do not know'. These items are conditionally administered based on current drinking status. No single unified CDE is appropriate; the ideal representation is a set of five distinct categorical CDEs, each with its own conditional eligibility criterion, question text, and defined response set as described above.

records.concept: Time-to-event (days) from study enrollment to stroke or censoring
records.idealCde: Time-to-event (survival analysis) variable for stroke: the number of days from study enrollment/baseline to either (a) the occurrence of a stroke event during follow-up, or (b) the last known follow-up date (censoring time) for participants who did not experience a stroke during the study period. Answers the question: 'How many days elapsed from study start until stroke or censoring?' Expected answer type: numeric, continuous; units: days.

gencde.title: Days from Study Enrollment to Stroke Event or Censoring
gencde.definition: The number of days elapsed from the date of study enrollment (baseline) to the date of a first stroke event during follow-up, or to the date of last known contact (censoring) for participants who did not experience a stroke during the study period.
gencde.questionText: How many days elapsed from study enrollment to the occurrence of a stroke event or, if no stroke occurred, to the last known follow-up date (censoring)?
relatedCdes: Adverse Event Study Intervention Date and Time
Cardiovascular event after spinal cord lesion date and time
Consensus on Grading Intracranial Flow Obstruction (COGIF) - follow-up date and time
gencde.rationale: Derived from MESA field ESP_stroke_tte_or_censor, which records days from study start to stroke (event=1) or last follow-up (event=0, censored). This is a standard right-censored survival analysis time variable. No permissible values are defined because the variable is continuous numeric. Minimum is 0 (event or censoring on enrollment day); no fixed maximum is imposed as it depends on study duration. Near-miss CDEs (adverse event dates, cardiovascular event dates, COGIF follow-up dates) were reviewed but represent date/time stamps rather than computed day-intervals and were not merged. UCUM unit 'd' (day) is used per convention.

All items are self-reported by the participant about themselves; answer types are categorical radio-button selections.

transforms.rationale: Both scales measure frequency of a negative emotional state over a similar recall window (past week). Mapping is approximate: source '0' (Rarely/none, <1 day) -> CDE '2' (Rarely); source '1' (Some/little, 1-2 days) -> CDE '3' (Sometimes); source '2' (Occasionally/moderate, 3-4 days) -> CDE '4' (Often); source '3' (All of the time, 5-7 days) -> CDE '5' (Always). CDE '1' (Never) has no direct source equivalent since the source scale's lowest option still implies some minimal occurrence. Confidence is moderate because the frequency bands overlap imperfectly and the source scale has no 'Never' category.

records.concept: Self-reported race and/or ethnicity or ancestry/ethnic origin (select all that apply, with free-text option)
records.idealCde: Race and/or Ethnicity: Captures the self-reported racial and/or ethnic identity of the participant, answering 'How would you describe your race and/or ethnicity or ancestry/ethnic origin?' Answer type is a combination of structured categorical selection (select all that apply) from a standardized value set — including American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian, Black or African American, Middle Eastern, North African, Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, White or Caucasian, and Other — plus an optional free-text field for specific ancestry or ethnic origin detail (e.g., Italian, Haitian, Cherokee, Korean). Source is self-report. The concept spans both broad racial categories and specific ethnic/ancestral origins, and the ideal CDE accommodates multi-select (check all that apply) as the primary response mode, with a single best-fit option as an alternative summary, and a free-text write-in for granular ancestry.

records.concept: Derived Hispanic ethnicity screening score (calculated field for demographics logic)
records.idealCde: Hispanic/Latino ethnicity identity: captures whether the respondent self-identifies as Hispanic, Latina/x, or of Spanish origin, and if so, which specific subgroup(s). Question asked of the participant about themselves: 'Are you of Hispanic, Latina/x, or Spanish origin? Check all that apply.' Answer type: multi-select categorical (select-all-that-apply checkbox); response options include: No; Yes – Mexican; Yes – Puerto Rican; Yes – Cuban; Yes – Dominican Republic; Yes – Central American; Yes – South American; Yes – Chicano/a/x; Yes – Other Hispanic/Latino/Spanish origin (specify); Prefer not to say. Unit: nominal category codes per selection. A derived numeric summary score (e.g., binary Hispanic yes/no flag) may be computed from the raw selections for use in screening or eligibility logic.

gencde.title: Derived Hispanic/Latino Ethnicity Screening Score (Calculated Demographics Field)
gencde.definition: A calculated numeric score derived from self-reported Hispanic, Latina/x, or Spanish origin identity responses, used internally in demographics screening logic to classify or flag participants as Hispanic/Latino for downstream analytic or eligibility purposes.
gencde.questionText: What is the calculated Hispanic ethnicity screening score derived from the participant's self-reported Hispanic, Latina/x, or Spanish origin identity responses?
relatedCdes: Hispanic origin
If "Other Hispanic/Latino", please specify
Is your child of Hispanic or Latino origin or descent?
gencde.rationale: Only one source field observed (AI-READI ethnicscore), typed as 'calc' with no explicit range or formula documented. The score is a derived/calculated field used in demographics screening logic rather than a directly collected self-report item; the IDEAL CDE describes the upstream multi-select categorical input from which this score is computed. Maximum value is left null because the scoring algorithm and upper bound are not specified in available source metadata. Near-miss CDEs (Hispanic origin, Other Hispanic/Latino specify, child Hispanic/Latino origin) represent related but distinct concepts — the parent self-report categorical and child-proxy variants — and are captured as aliases/relations only. Confidence is moderate due to single-cohort sourcing and absence of a published scoring formula.

records.concept: Self-reported gender identity (primary single-select + multi-select follow-up descriptors)
records.idealCde: Self-reported gender identity: A multi-component CDE capturing the participant's own gender identity. Primary question: 'What gender do you identify as?' with a single-select categorical response (e.g., Man [including transgender men], Woman [including transgender women], Non-binary, Other, Prefer not to say), supplemented by an optional multi-select follow-up allowing more specific or additional descriptors (e.g., Trans man/FTM, Trans woman/MTF, Genderqueer, Genderfluid, Transgender, or a free-text/additional-options pathway for those not represented). No qualifier on subject (self-report assumed from question phrasing). Answer type: categorical (radio for primary identity) plus categorical multi-select (checkbox for closer/additional descriptors). Note: sexual orientation (heterosexual/homosexual/bisexual) is a distinct concept present among the source fields and should be captured as a separate CDE — it is not part of gender identity.

transforms.rationale: Man maps to Male; Woman maps to Female; Non-binary and Other both map to 'Other, specify' as the CDE has no dedicated non-binary category. '777=Prefer not to say' is a missing-data/refusal sentinel with no equivalent CDE value — closest might be Unknown, but 'prefer not to say' is a deliberate refusal rather than truly unknown identity, so it is left unmapped to avoid misclassification.

Trans man (FTM) maps to Male and Trans woman (MTF) maps to Female as these reflect binary gender identity destinations. Genderqueer, Genderfluid, Gender variant, Two-spirit, and 'None of these/specify' all map to 'Other, specify' as the CDE has no non-binary categories. 'Questioning or unsure' maps to 'Unknown'. Note: mapping Trans man→Male and Trans woman→Female is a reasonable but debatable simplification; some use cases may prefer 'Other, specify' for all transgender identities, which lowers confidence slightly.

Man->Male and Woman->Female are direct matches. Non-binary, Transgender, and 'None of these/additional options' all map to 'Other, specify' as the only available CDE catch-all for non-binary/non-standard gender identities. 'Prefer not to answer' is a missing-data sentinel with no equivalent in the CDE value set (Unknown could be argued, but prefer-not-to-answer implies known refusal rather than truly unknown, so it is left unmapped). Confidence slightly reduced because the CDE lacks explicit non-binary/transgender codes and because the Unknown vs. prefer-not-to-answer distinction is ambiguous.

gencde.title: DXA AGC Scan Assumed Percentage of Lean Body Mass That Is Water
gencde.definition: The assumed percentage of lean body mass that is composed of water, as derived from a Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA) abdominal/general composition (AGC) scan, expressed as a decimal percentage.
gencde.questionText: What is the assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water as measured by the DXA AGC scan?
aliases: DXA lean mass water fraction AGC
AGC scan lean body mass water percentage
assumed lean body mass hydration fraction DXA
DXA-derived lean tissue water content percentage
lean body mass water assumption DXA abdominal general composition
relatedCdes: Dual X-ray absorptiometry whole body total lean value
Body mass index value
Body mass index category
gencde.rationale: Sourced from a single CLSA field (DXA_AGC_WATER_LBM_COM) typed as decimal. The AGC (abdominal/general composition) scan is distinct from the WBC (whole body composition) scan; this CDE captures only the AGC-derived value. The assumed water fraction of lean body mass is a fixed or model-derived constant used in DXA body composition algorithms (commonly ~73.2% in reference models), but is stored as a participant-level decimal field here. Near-miss CDEs (whole body lean value, BMI value, BMI category) were excluded as they represent distinct constructs. Confidence slightly reduced due to single-cohort sourcing and the specialized nature of the DXA algorithmic parameter.

gencde.title: DXA Whole Body Composition Scan Assumed Percentage of Lean Body Mass That Is Water
gencde.definition: The assumed percentage of lean body mass attributable to water, as derived from a dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) whole body composition (WBC) scan, expressed as a decimal percentage.
gencde.questionText: What is the assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water as measured by DXA whole body composition scan?
aliases: DXA WBC lean mass water fraction
whole body DXA lean body mass hydration percentage
DXA total body water percentage of lean mass
dual X-ray absorptiometry whole body lean mass water content percent
relatedCdes: Dual X-ray absorptiometry whole body total lean value
Body mass index value
Body mass index category
gencde.rationale: Sourced from a single CLSA field (DXA_WBC_WATER_LBM_COM) typed as decimal. This is a fixed physiological assumption constant (typically ~73.2% in standard DXA software such as Hologic) applied uniformly to all participants during lean mass estimation; it may vary slightly by software version or protocol. Distinct from the AGC-scan analogue of the same concept. Near-miss CDEs (whole body total lean value, BMI value, BMI category) were used only to confirm non-overlap and inform aliases. Minimum/maximum set to physiologically plausible bounds for a percentage; actual observed range in CLSA data is expected to be a narrow constant or near-constant value around 73%.

transforms.rationale: Source is labeled as a decimal (likely 0-1 range) representing a percentage, while target is in % units (0-100 range). Multiplying by 100 converts decimal fraction to percentage. However, if source is already stored as a percentage value (e.g., 73 rather than 0.73), the formula would just be 'source'. The 'decimal' type label suggests the 0-1 range interpretation. (llm_confidence 0.70)

gencde.title: Self-perception of body weight
gencde.definition: This term represents a patient's self-perception of their body weight in terms of being overweight or underweight. The term is based on, but not limited in use to, one of the questions in a two-item measure for an individual's weight change goals used in the Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS), is a national school-based survey conducted by CDC and state, territorial, tribal, and local education and health agencies as part of the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS). The YRBSS monitors health-related behaviors that contribute to the leading causes of death and disability among youth and adults.[https://www.cdc.gov/healthyyouth/data/yrbs/] For the other question item on what the individual is trying to do about their weight, use Body weight goal [LOINC: 90734-5].
gencde.rationale: The existing five-level value set already covers the concept but the source field uses a coarser three-category response (Overweight / Underweight / Just about right); adding these three codes alongside the existing values lets the CDE accommodate both granularities without removing any existing permissible values.

gencde.rationale: Sourced exclusively from MESA variable wtmodp5. The concept is a quality-control/data-collection flag indicating whether the standard operating procedure for weight measurement was altered for a given participant visit. Permissible values are strictly binary (No=0, Yes=1) as observed in the source field; no additional answer concepts were introduced. Near-miss CDEs (Body weight Measured, Body weight, Body weight Stated) relate to the weight value itself rather than to protocol fidelity, and are listed as aliases/relations only. The ideal CDE anchor describes a broader body-composition cluster; this GenCDE captures only the protocol-modification sub-element. Confidence is moderate because only one source cohort field was available for harmonization.

transforms.rationale: Code 1 (Direct entry) maps to Measured as it implies direct/objective measurement. Code 3 (Manual measurement of weight only) clearly maps to Measured. Code 2 (Manual entry of full results) is ambiguous but most plausibly represents self-reported or proxy-reported data entry rather than direct measurement, so mapped to Self-reported — though this is uncertain. Codes 4 (Not performed) and -1 (Question not asked) have no CDE equivalent and are unmapped. Confidence is moderate due to ambiguity of code 2. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:cfbdf5c3f11e1#g7): 5 of 5 source codes now map.

records.concept: Family history of asthma: which biological family members (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent) have had asthma
records.idealCde: Asthma diagnosis indicator: captures whether a person has been diagnosed with or reports having asthma, as well as which first-degree family members (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent) have had asthma. The self-report question is: 'Have you ever been told by a doctor or do you believe you have asthma?' answered as a binary yes/no (with an option for unknown/do not know: 0=No, 1=Yes, 9=Unknown). The family history question is: 'Which of your biological family members have had asthma? Select all that apply,' answered as a multi-select checklist of first-degree and second-degree relatives (Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent). Note: member fields carry two distinct subject qualifiers — self-report (index subject) and family-member report (multiple specified relatives) — both are preserved as components of this CDE.

records.concept: Snellen fraction visual acuity by laterality (OD/OS) and luminance condition (mesopic/photopic)
records.idealCde: Visual acuity expressed as a Snellen fraction, measured under both mesopic (low-light) and photopic (normal-light) luminance conditions, for each eye separately (right eye [OD] and left eye [OS]). The CDE answers: 'What is the Snellen fraction visual acuity for the specified eye under the specified lighting condition?' Answer type: text string representing a Snellen fraction (e.g., '20/20', '20/40'); qualifiers required: laterality (OD / OS) and luminance condition (mesopic / photopic).

gencde.title: Snellen Fraction Visual Acuity by Eye Laterality and Luminance Condition
gencde.definition: Visual acuity expressed as a Snellen fraction (e.g., '20/20') measured separately for the right eye (OD) and left eye (OS) under both mesopic (low-light, scotopic-to-photopic transition) and photopic (normal daylight) luminance conditions.
gencde.questionText: What is the Snellen fraction visual acuity for the specified eye (OD or OS) under the specified luminance condition (mesopic or photopic)?
relatedCdes: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) retinal thickness laterality type
Optical coherence tomography retinal nerve fiber layer thickness laterality type
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) macular cube laterality type
gencde.rationale: All four source fields (AI-READI viaodmsf, viaodpsf, viaosmsf, viaospsf) are text-typed Snellen fraction strings; no enumerated permissible values were observed, so the value domain is represented as free text constrained to the pattern '<numerator>/<denominator>' (e.g., '20/20', '20/40', '20/200'). Two qualifier axes are required: laterality (OD = right eye, OS = left eye) and luminance condition (mesopic = low-light ~0.1–3 cd/m², photopic = normal light ≥3 cd/m²). Near-miss CDEs relate only to OCT laterality typing and were used solely to confirm that no existing CDE covers this concept. Confidence is slightly below 1.0 because the exact Snellen denominator range and testing distance (typically 20 ft / 6 m) are not explicitly constrained in the source metadata.

records.concept: Change in time parent spends on care and supervision of children during school/childcare closure vs. in-person attendance
records.idealCde: Parental time change for child care/learning activities during school/childcare closure: Captures the self-reported change in time a parent/caregiver spends on a specified child-related activity (general care and supervision, OR helping with school/childcare-provided learning activities) compared to when the child was attending school or a childcare center in person. Question: 'Compared with when your child(ren) were attending school or a childcare center in person, how much time are you now spending on [care and supervision of your children / helping your children with learning activities provided by their school or childcare center]?' Answer type: Ordinal 5-point scale — Much more | A little more | About the same | A little less | Much less. Note: Two distinct sub-elements exist — one for general care/supervision and one for learning activity support — each using the same response scale and the same in-person attendance comparator.

records.concept: Gastrointestinal symptom (abdominal pain/discomfort/altered bowel habits) impact on life in general — 0–10 numeric scale
records.idealCde: Gastrointestinal symptom impact on daily life — a patient-reported outcome measuring the degree to which abdominal pain, discomfort, or altered bowel habits interfere with life in general. Question: 'How much are abdominal pain or discomfort or altered bowel habits affecting or interfering with your life in general?' Answer type: numeric integer or continuous scale from 0 to 10, where 0 = 'not at all' and 10 = 'completely'; collected via slider or discrete button selection.

gencde.title: Gastrointestinal Symptom Impact on Life in General (0–10 Scale)
gencde.definition: A patient-reported numeric rating (0–10) of the degree to which abdominal pain, discomfort, or altered bowel habits are affecting or interfering with the respondent's life in general, where 0 indicates no impact and 10 indicates complete interference.
gencde.questionText: Please indicate how much abdominal pain or discomfort or altered bowel habits are affecting or interfering with your life in general. (0 = Not at all; 10 = Completely)
aliases: IBS Severity Scoring System — life interference item
Abdominal symptom interference with daily life NRS
GI symptom life interference numeric rating scale
sourceVariables: UKBB:Degree to which abdominal pain/discomfort/altered bowel habits affect/interfere with life in general
relatedCdes: ROME I criteria abdominal pain discomfort type
In the past 7 days How much did pain interfere with your household chores?
How much did pain interfere with your day to day activities in past 7 days [PROMIS]
gencde.rationale: Derived from a single source cohort (UK Biobank), which itself adopted the item verbatim from the validated IBS Severity Scoring System (Francis et al., 1997). The numeric range 0–10 is fully observed in source data; the missing-data sentinel (-818 = Prefer not to answer) is excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per instructions. Data type is numeric integer (slider/button); although stored categorically in UKBB, the underlying construct and instrument are continuous ordinal, so numeric is the appropriate canonical type with min=0, max=10. Near-miss CDEs (ROME I abdominal pain type; PROMIS pain interference items) address related but distinct constructs and are listed only as contextual relations.

memberDetails.id: UKBB:Degree to which abdominal pain/discomfort/altered bowel habits affect/interfere with life in general
memberDetails.name: Degree to which abdominal pain/discomfort/altered bowel habits affect/interfere with life in general
memberDetails.text:
Question asked: "Please indicate how much abdominal pain or discomfort or altered bowel habits are affecting or interfering with your life in general."

Participants were asked to move a slider to choose a number between 0 to 10, with 0 meaning "not at all" and 10 meaning "completely". Participants using an older browser were asked to select a button from 0 to 10.

The question in this field was taken from the IBS Severity Scoring System used with the authors' permission.

Francis CY, Morris J, Whorwell PJ. The irritable bowel severity scoring system: a simple method of monitoring irritable bowel syndrome and its progress. Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics 1997;11(2):395-402

transforms.rationale: The source is a 4-point CES-D style scale while the target CDE has 5 points (Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Often, Always). The source code 0 'Rarely or none of the time' collapses what the CDE separates into 'Never' and 'Rarely', so it is mapped to 'Rarely' as the closest match, leaving 'Never' without a source equivalent. The remaining three source codes map reasonably well to Sometimes/Often/Always by frequency progression. The missing 'Never' category and the collapsed lowest category reduce confidence.

The source appears to be a CES-D style scale with 4 frequency options mapped to a 5-point PROMIS-style scale. 'Rarely or none of the time' maps to Rarely (Never is unrepresented in source). 'Some or little of the time' maps to Sometimes. 'Moderate amount of time' maps to Often. 'Most of the time' maps to Always. The source has no equivalent for 'Never', and the boundaries between categories are approximate, reducing confidence slightly.

gencde.title: Total Intentional Exercise Energy Expenditure Over Last 7 Days (MET-min/wk, Monday–Sunday)
gencde.definition: The total volume of intentional exercise energy expenditure accumulated across all exercise types during the past 7 days (Monday through Sunday), expressed in MET-minutes per week, derived from structured physical activity questionnaire items.

gencde.rationale: Both MESA source fields (exercm1c and exercm5c) capture total intentional exercise across all types (Q9–15) over a Monday–Sunday 7-day window and are numeric MET-min/wk measures; the unit label discrepancy ('MET-min/wk' vs 'Min/Wk') in the source metadata is treated as a labeling inconsistency — both fields are harmonized to MET-min/wk based on the variable name and concept context. No upper bound is imposed as extreme outliers are possible in athletic populations; downstream quality control should flag implausible values (e.g., >10,000 MET-min/wk). The near-miss CDEs (exercise intensity type, exercise minute average, exercise engagement indicator) are related but distinct constructs. The ideal CDE anchor describes moderate-intensity activity specifically, but the source fields capture all intentional exercise types; the GenCDE is therefore scoped to all-intensity total intentional exercise to faithfully represent the source data.

transforms.rationale: All nine income bracket source codes map directly to their CDE equivalents by label (minor whitespace differences are inconsequential). PMI_PreferNotToAnswer ('Prefer not to answer') has no corresponding value in the CDE value set and is therefore unmapped.

Source codes 1-3 all fall within 'Less than $10,000' (covering <$5K, $5K-$7,999, $8K-$11,999 — note code 3 slightly straddles the $10K boundary but majority falls below). Codes 4-6 map to '$10,000-$24,999'. Codes 7-8 map to '$25,000-$34,999'. Codes 9-10 map to '$35,000-$49,999'. Codes 11-12 map cleanly. Code 13 ('$100,000 or more') is mapped to '$100,000-$149,999' as the closest lower bound, but it could also represent $150K-$199K or $200K+; this is the main source of uncertainty. The CDE has finer granularity at the top end that cannot be recovered from the source. Confidence slightly reduced due to boundary overlap for code 3 and the collapsed top category for code 13.

Most source codes map cleanly into CDE brackets. Key ambiguities: (1) Source code 3 ($8,000-$11,999) straddles the CDE boundary of $10,000, but the majority of its range falls below $10,000 so mapped to 'Less than $10,000'. (2) Source code 15 ($150,000 or more) is mapped to '$150,000-$199,999' but it could also include $200,000+; since the source does not distinguish above $150,000, this is the best available mapping but introduces some uncertainty. All other mappings are straightforward containment within CDE ranges.

gencde.rationale: This CDE represents a single binary indicator within a multi-select battery of household income source items. The two observed source fields (INC_SRCE_IN_TRM for employment/wages and INC_SRCE_SE_TRM for self-employment) share identical question text and value domains (1=Yes, 0=No), confirming a repeated-measure pattern across income source categories. The canonical permissible values are restricted to Yes/No as observed; no additional source categories are introduced. Implementers should instantiate one instance of this CDE per income source category assessed (e.g., wages/salary, self-employment, government transfers, pensions, investments). Near-miss CDEs (Annual Household Income Range, Household Member Size, food insecurity skip-meal item) were excluded as they capture distinct constructs. Confidence is modestly reduced because only two source-specific indicators were provided, limiting full enumeration of the intended multi-select battery.

gencde.title: Perceived Adequacy of Household Income and Investments for Retirement
gencde.definition: A self-reported assessment of whether the respondent believes their household income and investments will be sufficient to maintain their current standard of living upon retirement.
gencde.questionText: When you retire, how adequate do you think your household income and investments will be to maintain your standard of living?
relatedCdes: Household Member Size
Household income
Shared Living Space Number of Individuals
gencde.rationale: Sourced from a single CLSA field (RPL_STDLIV_TRM). The ideal CDE anchor describes a broader household income/composition profile, but the sole observed source field measures only the subjective retirement income adequacy construct; the GenCDE is scoped accordingly. Three permissible values are retained exactly as observed (Adequate, Barely adequate, Inadequate) with ordinal codes 1–3 reflecting increasing inadequacy. Near-miss CDEs (Household Member Size, Household income, Shared Living Space) are related but distinct constructs. Confidence is moderate (0.82) given single-cohort sourcing and slight mismatch between the ideal CDE anchor and the actual observed concept.

gencde.title: Time Elapsed Since Interview Start at Blood Pressure Screen Presentation (Seconds)
gencde.definition: The number of seconds elapsed from the start of the assessment interview to the moment the blood pressure measurement screen was displayed, used to calculate the inter-measurement interval between successive blood pressure readings.
gencde.questionText: How many seconds had elapsed since the start of the interview when the blood pressure screen was shown?
aliases: time from interview start to blood pressure measurement
sourceVariables: UKBB:Time since interview start at which blood pressure screen(s) shown
relatedCdes: Blood time collection storage interval
Contextual and Cue Fear Conditioning - Between tone and shock delivery interval
CCHD newborn screening protocol used [Type]
gencde.rationale: Concept is derived solely from the UK Biobank field capturing integer seconds since interview start at which the blood pressure screen was shown. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes diastolic BP itself, which is a near-miss; the true concept here is a procedural timing variable used to derive the interval between bp1 and bp2 readings. No permissible values apply; data type is numeric integer, unit is seconds (UCUM: s), minimum is 0 (cannot precede interview start), and no validated upper bound is specified in source data. Near-miss CDEs (blood collection storage interval, fear conditioning tone-shock interval) confirm the 'elapsed time interval' semantic neighborhood but are contextually distinct. Confidence is slightly reduced because only one source cohort (UKBB) contributes to this concept.

records.concept: PHQ: Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless in past 2 weeks (4-point scale)

cde.id: Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) Last Two Weeks How Often Feel Depressed Score 4 Point Scale

records.idealCde: Depression symptom burden and history: A composite concept capturing (1) frequency of depressive symptoms over the past 2 weeks — specifically low mood/hopelessness and sleep disturbance — rated on a 4-point ordinal scale (Not at all / Several days / More than half the days / Nearly every day); (2) cumulative depressive symptom severity as a numeric total score on the CES-D (Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale); (3) lifetime history of a sustained depressive episode — binary categorical question 'Have you ever had a period of feeling depressed or down for at least a whole week?' (Yes / No / Do not know / Prefer not to answer); and (4) duration of the longest such lifetime depressive episode in weeks (integer, range 1–999), collected only among those who endorsed lifetime depression. Answer types: ordinal frequency ratings (4-level scale) for past-2-week symptom items; numeric sum score for CES-D total; categorical (Yes/No/Do not know/Prefer not to answer) for lifetime episode presence; positive integer (weeks) for longest episode duration.

gencde.title: Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) Total Score
gencde.definition: A numeric composite score derived from the 20-item Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), reflecting the overall frequency and severity of depressive symptoms experienced by the respondent during the past week, with higher scores indicating greater depressive symptom burden.
gencde.questionText: What is the total score on the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), summing all item responses rated on a 0–3 frequency scale over the past week?
aliases: Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale total score

Center for Epidemiologic Studies-Depression Scale (CES-D) - unfriendly indicator
gencde.rationale: The CES-D is a validated 20-item self-report instrument (Radloff, 1977) in which each item is scored 0–3 (rarely/none of the time to most/all of the time), yielding a total range of 0–60; a score ≥16 is the conventional clinical cut-point for significant depressive symptomatology. The source field MESA:cesd5c is a numeric CES-D total score variable. Near-miss CDEs represent individual CES-D item indicators (sadness, depressed, unfriendly) rather than the composite total; they are retained as related concepts. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a broader composite concept including PHQ-style 2-week frequency items and a lifetime history binary item, which are distinct from the CES-D total score; this GenCDE is scoped specifically to the CES-D numeric total as observed in the source field.

records.concept: Number of periods of feeling depressed or down for at least one week (lifetime count)
records.idealCde: Depression symptom burden and history: A composite concept capturing (1) frequency of depressive symptoms over the past 2 weeks — specifically low mood/hopelessness and sleep disturbance — rated on a 4-point ordinal scale (Not at all / Several days / More than half the days / Nearly every day); (2) cumulative depressive symptom severity as a numeric total score on the CES-D (Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale); (3) lifetime history of a sustained depressive episode — binary categorical question 'Have you ever had a period of feeling depressed or down for at least a whole week?' (Yes / No / Do not know / Prefer not to answer); and (4) duration of the longest such lifetime depressive episode in weeks (integer, range 1–999), collected only among those who endorsed lifetime depression. Answer types: ordinal frequency ratings (4-level scale) for past-2-week symptom items; numeric sum score for CES-D total; categorical (Yes/No/Do not know/Prefer not to answer) for lifetime episode presence; positive integer (weeks) for longest episode duration.

records.idealCde: Walking and stair-climbing difficulty/inability: captures whether an individual experiences difficulty or complete inability performing ambulatory tasks including walking alone up and down a flight of stairs, walking 2–3 neighborhood blocks, and/or climbing stairs generally. Question: 'Do you have difficulty or are you unable to walk (including climbing stairs and walking short distances in your neighborhood)?' Answer type: categorical/ordinal — options include No difficulty, Yes difficulty, Unable to do, Do not do on doctor's orders, Prefer not to answer. No specific laterality, body site, or time-window qualifier is specified; fields vary in granularity from a single global walking/stair-climbing item to task-specific sub-items (stairs vs. blocks vs. general ambulation), so the ideal CDE should accommodate both a summary-level response and task-specific sub-questions within the same construct.

records.concept: Family history of mental health or substance use conditions (blood relatives) — multi-select checklist of condition categories

cde.id: Family health problems psychological history type

records.idealCde: Family history of mental health or substance use conditions (blood relatives): a multi-part CDE set capturing (1) which mental health or substance use conditions (e.g., alcohol use disorder, anxiety/panic disorder, depression, autism spectrum disorder, and others) have been diagnosed in the participant's blood relatives — answered as a multi-select checklist of condition categories; (2) for each endorsed condition, which specific biological family members are affected (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, etc.) — answered as a multi-select checklist of relationship types per condition; and (3) the participant's own age at first diagnosis of any other (unspecified) mental health or substance use condition — answered as an ordinal radio selection (Child 0–11, Adolescent 12–17, Adult 18–64, or older adult category). Answer types: checkbox (multi-select) for condition presence and affected relatives; ordinal categorical for self-reported age-at-diagnosis of residual conditions. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified; context is self-reported family history by blood relation.

transforms.rationale: This is a positively-worded CES-D item (feeling hopeful about the future) where the source uses a reversed numeric coding (3=Rarely, 0=All of the time) compared to the CDE's standard coding (0=Rarely, 3=Most/all of the time). All four frequency categories align perfectly in meaning after reversing the numeric codes. The slight confidence reduction accounts for the minor wording difference ('All of the time' vs 'Most or all of the time') in the highest frequency category, though these are functionally equivalent in CES-D scoring practice.

The source uses a reversed 1-4 scale (All of the time=1 down to Rarely/never=4) while the CDE uses 0-3 (Rarely=0 up to Most/all=3). The frequency labels align perfectly when reversed: source 1->CDE 3, source 2->CDE 2, source 3->CDE 1, source 4->CDE 0. Note that this item is a positive/hopeful item on the CES-D, so the reversal is expected in scoring.

records.concept: DASH Diet adherence score including sodium (0-9 points)
records.idealCde: DASH Diet adherence score (sodium-inclusive version): captures the degree to which an individual's dietary pattern conforms to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet, including sodium intake as a scored component. The question answered is: 'What is the individual's total DASH diet score when sodium consumption is included as a scored dietary component?' Answer type: numeric integer or continuous score on a 0–9 point scale, where higher scores indicate greater adherence to the DASH dietary pattern (including sodium restriction).

gencde.title: DASH Diet Adherence Score Including Sodium (0–9 Points)
gencde.definition: A composite numeric score quantifying an individual's adherence to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) dietary pattern, with sodium intake included as a scored component, yielding a total score ranging from 0 to 9 where higher values indicate greater adherence.
gencde.questionText: What is the individual's total DASH diet adherence score when sodium consumption is included as a scored dietary component?

relatedCdes: Overall diet health scale
Sodium level unit of measure

gencde.rationale: Derived from the MESA cohort variable dash_sodium1. The DASH diet score is typically constructed by scoring 8 dietary components (fruits, vegetables, nuts/legumes, whole grains, low-fat dairy, red/processed meats, sweetened beverages, sodium); the sodium-inclusive version explicitly scores sodium restriction as one of the 9 possible points. Each component contributes 0 or 1 point based on whether intake meets DASH targets, yielding an integer range of 0–9. Near-miss CDEs (overall diet health scale, sodium level unit of measure, SDoH score) were excluded as they do not capture DASH-specific multi-component dietary adherence. Score may be treated as integer or continuous depending on analytic context.

records.concept: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication) structured symptom assessment (Rose/Edinburgh Questionnaire items)

cde.id: Do you suffer from intermittent claudication [PhenX]

records.idealCde: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication) symptom assessment: a structured set of binary and categorical items characterizing walking-induced leg or buttock pain, including (1) presence of pain in leg or buttock while walking (Yes/No), (2) anatomical location of pain — whether it includes the calf/calves (Pain includes calf/calves | Pain does not include calf/calves), (3) whether leg pain ever disappears while continuing to walk (Yes/No), (4) predominant side of leg pain (Right | Left | Both), and (5) whether leg pain occurs when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground (Yes/No). Collectively these items screen for intermittent claudication consistent with peripheral arterial disease. Answer types are binary (0=No/1=Yes) or nominal categorical as specified; no continuous units required.

Direct binary mapping: source 0=NO maps to CDE 'No', source 1=YES maps to CDE 'Yes'. No 'Don't know' equivalent exists in the source, but all source codes are confidently mapped.

Both source codes describe leg pain (with or without calf involvement), which could indicate intermittent claudication. However, classic intermittent claudication specifically involves calf pain, so code 1 (pain includes calf) maps more confidently to 'Yes' for claudication. Code 2 (pain does not include calf) is ambiguous — it may represent atypical claudication or non-claudication leg pain. Neither code maps to 'No' or 'Don't know' since both describe presence of pain. Confidence is low because the source variable appears to be a sub-question about pain location rather than a direct yes/no claudication screening question, and mapping code 2 to 'Yes' for claudication is uncertain.

The source variable captures which leg(s) are affected by claudication (Right Side, Left Side, Both Legs), while the target CDE is a yes/no/don't-know question about whether the person suffers from intermittent claudication. Although the source codes imply a positive claudication finding (presence of claudication in specific legs), they do not directly map to the Yes/No/Don't Know response options. One could argue all three source codes imply 'Yes', but the source variable appears to be a follow-up question asked only of those who already confirmed claudication, making a direct mapping ambiguous and potentially incorrect without knowing the full survey context. All source codes are left unmapped.

The source variable captures duration of claudication symptoms (10 minutes or less vs. more than 10 minutes), which is a severity/duration sub-question asked after confirming claudication presence. It does not map to the Yes/No/Don't know response options of the target CDE, which asks whether the person suffers from intermittent claudication at all. No confident mapping is possible without additional context.

records.concept: Age at first diagnosis of personal circulatory condition (CHF / CAD) in life-stage categories
records.idealCde: Circulatory condition history — a cluster of CDEs capturing both personal and family history of specific circulatory conditions (congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease, heart attack). For personal history: age at first diagnosis reported in life-stage categories (Child 0–11, Adolescent 12–17, Adult 18–64, Older Adult 65+); answer type is ordinal categorical radio selection, one per condition. For family history: which biological relatives (Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, and potentially others) have had each named condition; answer type is multi-select checkbox (select all that apply), one set per condition. The personal-history fields are self-reported (subject = self); the family-history fields are reported by the participant about their biological family members. Conditions covered include at minimum: congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease (including angina), and heart attack.

gencde.rationale: This CDE is a compound multi-select element that simultaneously encodes both the affected biological relative (REL_01–REL_06) and the specific circulatory condition (COND_01–COND_14). In the source AoU fields, relative and condition are cross-tabulated per condition-specific checkbox question; the omnibus field (diagnosedhealthcondition_circulatorycondition) captures condition type only without specifying relative. The canonical permissible-value set merges both dimensions into a single flat list to support harmonized storage; downstream analysis should treat relative codes and condition codes as paired attributes. Missing-data sentinels (Don't know, Prefer not to answer) observed in the omnibus source field are excluded per schema instructions. 'None of the above' is retained as a substantive negative response. Near-miss CDEs were used only to inform aliases.

transforms.rationale: Each source code encodes both a family member relationship and a condition (Congestive Heart Failure). The CDE separates relationship codes (REL_*) and condition codes (COND_*) as independent values. The source codes are mapped to their respective relationship codes (REL_01 through REL_06) since the condition component (Congestive Heart Failure = COND_01) is uniform across all source codes and cannot be expressed as a single combined mapping. A full harmonization would require emitting both a REL_* and COND_01 code per source record; this mapping captures the relationship dimension only. Confidence is slightly reduced due to the structural mismatch between the composite source encoding and the CDE's separate relationship/condition value sets.

Each source code encodes both a family member relationship and a condition (Coronary Artery/Heart Disease). The CDE appears to be a multi-dimensional instrument capturing both relationship (REL_xx) and condition (COND_xx) axes. The source codes map cleanly to the relationship codes (REL_01 through REL_06), and the embedded condition 'CoronaryArteryHeartDisease' aligns with COND_02. However, since each source code conflates both dimensions and the CDE separates them, a full lossless mapping would require also emitting COND_02 for each record. The relationship mapping is provided here; COND_02 should be applied as a constant condition value for all these source codes in the harmonization pipeline. Confidence is slightly reduced due to this structural mismatch.

Each source code encodes both a family member relationship and a specific condition (Heart Attack = COND_03). The CDE appears to be a multi-dimensional element covering both relationship (REL_*) and condition (COND_*) axes. The source codes map cleanly to the relationship codes (REL_01 through REL_06). The condition component (Heart Attack -> COND_03) is implicit in all source codes but cannot be expressed as a single target code mapping since the CDE separates relationship and condition into distinct value sets. Mapping is made to the relationship dimension only; the Heart Attack condition (COND_03) is a fixed implicit value for all these source codes and would need to be handled as a separate field or noted in transformation logic.

All six source codes encode the same condition (Heart Valve Disease) but vary by family-member relationship. Each maps cleanly to the corresponding REL_* code for the relationship. The condition itself (Heart Valve Disease = COND_04) is implicit in the variable name/context rather than a separate selectable dimension in the source, so no COND code mapping is needed here — the source variable is scoped to heart valve disease already. Confidence slightly below 1.0 because the CDE appears to be a combined relationship+condition structure, and it is possible the intended mapping should also include COND_04; however, based on the source codes provided, only relationship values are being coded.

Each source code encodes both a family member relationship and a condition (High Blood Pressure). The CDE appears to be a combined relationship+condition matrix. The relationship portion maps cleanly to REL_01 through REL_06. However, the condition portion (HighBloodPressure = COND_05) is embedded in the source code name but the CDE treats relationships and conditions as separate value codes. Since the source codes are scoped to a single variable representing 'who has high blood pressure', the relationship codes are the most direct mapping. The COND_05 (High Blood Pressure) aspect is implicit in the variable context rather than the code value itself. Confidence is moderate because the CDE may expect compound relationship+condition codes or separate axes, and the mapping discards the condition dimension.

All condition codes map directly and unambiguously to CDE condition codes by label. PMI_None maps to NONE. PMI_DontKnow and PMI_PreferNotToAnswer are missing-data/refusal sentinels with no equivalent in the CDE value set. The CDE also contains relationship codes (REL_01–REL_06) which have no corresponding source values in this source variable.

records.idealCde: Home-based exercise frequency — captures how often an individual engages in home exercise activities (e.g., stretching, calisthenics, yoga, muscle-strengthening exercises such as weight lifting or push-ups) performed at home. Question: 'How often do you engage in home exercise?' Expected answer: ordinal frequency category or numeric count of sessions per week/over the past 7 days (e.g., daily/almost daily, once or twice a week, rarely or never, prefer not to say); qualifier: home setting, self-reported, general or recent 7-day recall window.

gencde.title: Muscle-Strengthening Exercise Frequency Over Past 7 Days (Day Count)
gencde.definition: A self-reported numeric count of the number of days in the past 7 days on which an individual performed exercises specifically intended to increase muscle strength and endurance, such as weight lifting, push-ups, or similar resistance activities.
gencde.questionText: Over the past 7 days, how many days did you do any exercises specifically to increase muscle strength and endurance, such as lifting weights or push-ups?
relatedCdes: In the past 7 days How often did you have to push yourself to get things done because of your fatigue?
In the past 7 days How often did you have to force yourself to get up and do things because of your fatigue?
In the past 7 days How often did you have enough energy to exercise strenuously?
gencde.rationale: The single source field (CLSA PA2_EXER_MCQ) is free-text but conceptually captures a 0–7 day count over a 7-day recall window; the numeric data type and 0–7 range are imposed by the 7-day recall frame. The ideal CDE anchor described ordinal frequency categories, but the source field wording ('how often … over the past 7 days') and the CLSA codebook convention support a raw day-count integer response. If ordinal categories (e.g., 0 days, 1–2 days, 3–4 days, 5–7 days) are encountered in derived variables, a categorical sibling CDE should be created. Near-miss CDEs relate to fatigue-driven effort and energy for exercise, not muscle-strengthening frequency, and were excluded from permissible values but inform alias vocabulary.

gencde.rationale: Concept is strictly dietary/nutritional glucose intake (grams, 24-hour recall), as observed in the UKBB 'Glucose' field. transforms.rationale: Most source codes map cleanly to CDE values. The main ambiguity is InsuranceTypeUpdate_VA (VA health care specifically) and InsuranceTypeUpdate_Military (TRICARE/military), which both map to the single CDE option 'TRICARE or other military health care, including VA health care' — the CDE consolidates these two into one category. InsuranceTypeUpdate_None ('self-pay / no insurance') maps to 'Uninsured' as the closest equivalent, though self-pay is not strictly the same as uninsured. Confidence slightly reduced due to these two consolidation/nuance issues. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:cca73c5d06ef2#g1): 5 of 9 source codes now map.

transforms.rationale: The source variable only captures whether someone is covered or not covered (plus missing-data sentinels), while the TARGET CDE asks about the specific *type* of health insurance. There is no meaningful one-to-one mapping: '1=Covered' could correspond to any of the insured CDE categories (employer, direct purchase, Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE, IHS, or other), and '0=Not Covered' is closest to 'Uninsured' but cannot be confidently mapped without additional context confirming the question intent. '999=Not Sure' and '777=Prefer not to say' are missing-data sentinels with no CDE equivalents. All codes are placed in unmapped.

records.concept: Dietary frequency of beans/legumes, chicken, or fish (times per week)
records.idealCde: Dietary frequency of a specific food or food group: captures how often an individual consumes a designated food item or category (e.g., beans/legumes, poultry/fish, or added fats such as butter/margarine) within a defined reference period (typically per week or per day). The question asked is: 'How often do you usually eat [specified food/food group]?' Expected answer type: ordinal frequency category (e.g., never, less than once per week, 1–2 times per week, 3 or more times per week) or a continuous decimal value representing times per day/week, depending on administration format; a 'Prefer not to answer' option should be available. Units: eating occasions per week (or per day for continuous format). Note: member fields carry different food-item qualifiers (protein-rich foods [beans, chicken, fish] vs. added fats [butter/margarine on bread or cooked vegetables]), indicating this concept spans multiple food-specific frequency items rather than a single unified qualifier.

Original codes (0, 1, 2, 777) were remapped to clean sequential codes (1, 2, 3) for frequency categories and 999 for the non-response sentinel 'Prefer not to say'; the non-response sentinel is retained as a permissible value per source data but should be treated as missing in analytic contexts. gencde.title: Dietary Frequency of Butter or Regular Margarine on Bread or Cooked Vegetables
gencde.definition: A self-reported measure of how often an individual usually consumes butter or regular margarine applied to bread or cooked vegetables, expressed as a continuous decimal value representing frequency per day or per week.

gencde.rationale: The sole source field (CLSA NUT_BTTR_NB_COM) uses a continuous decimal type, so the CDE is modeled as numeric rather than ordinal categorical. The unit is assumed to be times per week consistent with CLSA dietary frequency conventions; no explicit maximum is imposed as very high values are physiologically possible but rare. Near-miss CDEs (NHANES-style FFQ items) confirm the concept domain but use ordinal categories and distinguish bread from vegetables; the CLSA field combines both surfaces into one item, which is preserved here. If future cohorts contribute ordinal response options, the data type may be revised to categorical.

records.concept: Specific diabetes management modality (oral pills, non-insulin injectables, insulin, lifestyle changes)
records.idealCde: Diabetes management modality: A set of distinct CDEs capturing the specific methods a person uses to manage their blood glucose and A1C levels, covering five domains: (1) Oral glucose-lowering medication use — 'Do you take oral pills to control your blood glucose/A1C levels?' — binary Yes/No; (2) Non-insulin injectable medication use (e.g., GLP-1 receptor agonists, amylin analogs) — 'Do you use non-insulin injectable medications to control your blood glucose levels?' — binary Yes/No; (3) Insulin injection use — 'Do you inject insulin to control your blood glucose levels?' — binary Yes/No; (4) Lifestyle modification use (diet, exercise, consistent eating schedule) — 'Do you use lifestyle changes to control your blood glucose/A1C levels?' — binary Yes/No; (5) Diabetes health education engagement frequency — 'How often do you engage in diabetes health education activities (e.g., dietician consultation, support groups, educational media, apps)?' — ordinal categorical: Rarely or never / Occasionally (every 2–3 months) / Regularly at least monthly. All items are self-reported and pertain to the respondent's own current diabetes management practices, with no laterality or site qualifier.

transforms.rationale: Several mappings are imperfect: COPE_A_106 covers both part-time and full-time but is mapped to 'Employed part time' as the best partial fit (full-time is separately captured by self-employed); COPE_A_186 (self-employed) is mapped to 'Employed full time' as the closest available CDE option, though self-employment is a distinct category not explicitly in the CDE; COPE_A_153 and COPE_A_61 both map to 'Unemployed' losing duration granularity; COPE_A_196 (Retired) maps to 'Retired due to age/preference' as the generic retirement option, though reason is unknown; COPE_A_128 (Unable to work/disabled) maps to 'Retired due to disability' as the closest CDE equivalent; COPE_A_30 (Prefer not to answer) is a missing-data sentinel with no CDE equivalent.

Homemaker, Student, and Unable to work (disabled) map cleanly. Retired maps to 'Retired due to age/preference' as the default retirement category, though intent is uncertain. 'Employed for wages' bundles part-time and full-time into one code, so it cannot be split into 'Employed full time' vs 'Employed part time' without additional data. Self-employed has no CDE equivalent. Both 'Out of work' codes could map to 'Unemployed' but neither distinguishes disability vs. preference, and the CDE's 'Unemployed' label is ambiguous relative to 'Retired due to disability'; left unmapped to avoid misclassification. 'Prefer not to answer' is a missing-data sentinel with no CDE equivalent.

Code 8 (retired not working) maps to 'Retired due to age/preference' as the best fit, though disability retirement cannot be distinguished without more info. Code 5 (employed on-leave, non-health) has no clear CDE equivalent — it is a leave of absence but not medical, and the CDE only has 'Medical leave of absence'. Code 9 (retired but working) is ambiguous — could be part-time employed or retired, no clean CDE match. Code 10 (retired volunteering) does not fit any CDE code precisely since volunteering is not employment and the retirement reason is unspecified.

records.concept: Geographic access to services deprivation domain (food shop, GP, school, post office, library by walking or public bus)
records.idealCde: Government-sponsored health insurance coverage status: A binary indicator capturing whether an individual is currently covered by Medicaid, Medical Assistance (MA), the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), or any other state or government-sponsored health plan based on income or disability. Question: 'Are you currently covered by Medicaid, Medical Assistance (MA), CHIP, or any kind of state or government-sponsored health plan based on income or a disability?' Answer type: Categorical radio; values: 1=Covered, 0=Not Covered, 999=Not Sure, 777=Prefer not to say. Note: Source concept also includes a distinct geographic access deprivation domain measuring household-level walkability/public-transit accessibility to essential services (food shop, GP surgery, primary school, post office, public library); these two constructs represent different qualifiers and measurement targets and should be treated as separate CDEs rather than harmonized into one.

gencde.title: Geographic Access to Services Deprivation Domain Score (Walking or Public Bus)
gencde.definition: A continuous composite score quantifying the degree of deprivation arising from a household's inability to access essential day-to-day services—including food shops, GP surgeries, primary and secondary schools, post offices, public libraries, leisure centres, NHS dentists, and transport nodes—by walking or public bus, as derived from government area-level deprivation indices (e.g., Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation).
gencde.questionText: What is the geographic access to services deprivation score for this individual's area of residence, reflecting difficulty reaching essential local services (food shop, GP surgery, school, post office, library, leisure centre, NHS dentist, and transport nodes) by walking or public bus?
aliases: Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation – Access to Services domain
WHOQOL-BREF health access domain (near-miss relation only)
relatedCdes: World Health Organization Quality of Life (WHOQOL-BREF) - health access scale
Dependent children living in household number
Parent dependent children living in household number
gencde.rationale: Source field is the UK Biobank 'Access to services score (Wales)', a continuous area-level composite derived from the Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation (WIMD) Access to Services domain. The score is dimensionless (standardised/ranked within the Welsh WIMD framework); exact observed min/max are not fixed across releases and are left null pending cohort-specific documentation. The ideal CDE anchor provided (government-sponsored health insurance) is unrelated to this concept and was disregarded. Near-miss CDEs (WHOQOL-BREF health access, household children counts) were used only to confirm non-overlap and to populate aliases. No permissible values are listed because the variable is continuous. Units are recorded as '1' (dimensionless ratio/index score per UCUM convention).

memberDetails.name: Access to services score (Wales)
memberDetails.text:
The purpose of this domain is to illustrate the deprivation as a result of a household's inability to access a range of services, considered necessary for day-to-day living. The access is by walking or using public bus services or both. The indicators used for the geographical access to services domain were:
  • Food shop
  • GP surgery
  • Primary school
  • Post office
  • Public library
  • Leisure centre
  • NHS dentist
  • Secondary school
  • Transport nodes

cde.id: Have your menstrual periods stopped permanently [PhenX]

records.idealCde: Permanent menstrual cessation status: Captures whether the respondent's menstrual periods have stopped permanently. Question: 'Have your menstrual periods stopped permanently?' Answer type: Categorical (enumerated); values: (1) No, periods have not stopped; (2) Yes, no menstrual periods at all; (3) Yes, but periods are induced by hormones; (4) Not sure. Self-reported by the participant. No laterality or body-site qualifier. Applicable to individuals who have ever menstruated.
