gencde.rationale: Three source fields from AI-READI were harmonized: icf_dat (date form opened, text type), icfcmpts (completion timestamp, text type), and icfsvyts (start timestamp, text type). All capture temporal metadata for the informed consent instrument. Because the source fields distinguish 'opened/started' from 'completed', implementations should instantiate this CDE twice when both events are recorded — once with qualifier 'start' and once with qualifier 'completion'. Values should be stored as ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) or datetime (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss); source fields are typed as text, so downstream ETL must validate and cast. Near-miss CDEs 'Informed Consent Signed Date' and 'Date form completed' were used to inform aliases but were not matched because they do not capture the survey-instrument context or the start-vs-completion distinction present in the source fields.

records.concept: Family history of diabetes (by relative and diabetes type)
records.idealCde: Family and personal history of diabetes (any type): a set of CDEs capturing (1) whether the respondent's first-degree relatives (mother, father, sibling, son, daughter) have been diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes, Type 2 diabetes, or other/unknown diabetes — answered per relative via multi-select checkbox or per-relative yes/no radio (values: Yes | No | Unknown | Prefer not to say); (2) whether either parent specifically has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes (radio: Yes | No | Unknown | Prefer not to say); (3) whether a sibling specifically has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes (radio: Yes | No | Unknown | Prefer not to say); and (4) the respondent's own age at first diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes, captured as an ordinal life-stage category (Child [0–11] | Adolescent [12–17] | Adult [18–64] | Older Adult [65–74] | 75+). The concept spans self-reported personal diagnosis age and first-degree family history across three diabetes subtypes (Type 1, Type 2, other/unknown), with the subject qualifier varying across fields: self (age at diagnosis), parents as a pair, individual first-degree relatives (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son).

gencde.title: Dietary Cholesterol Intake from Past 24 Hours (mg)
gencde.definition: The estimated total amount of cholesterol consumed through diet in the preceding 24-hour period, expressed in milligrams, as derived from a dietary recall or food frequency assessment.
gencde.questionText: What was your total dietary cholesterol intake (in mg) over the past 24 hours?
relatedCdes: Past current cardiovascular cholesterol type text
High cholesterol treatment type
Total cholesterol value
gencde.rationale: Concept is unambiguously a continuous numeric dietary intake variable (mg) from a 24-hour recall, as evidenced by the single UKBB source field. The ideal CDE anchor describes blood/serum cholesterol measurement and classification, which is a distinct clinical concept; it was used only to confirm non-overlap and to inform alias terms (e.g., 'Total cholesterol value' as a near-miss). No permissible values are applicable for a continuous numeric measure. Upper bound is left null because extreme but valid dietary cholesterol values are not formally capped in dietary recall instruments; lower bound is 0 (no cholesterol consumed). Confidence is slightly reduced from 1.0 due to the single source cohort (UKBB only) and absence of corroborating cohort fields.

records.concept: Respondent's highest educational attainment (level/degree completed)

No laterality, body-site, or condition qualifier is present; the subject is the respondent (self). Units: none (categorical ordinal).

transforms.rationale: numeric variable with no declared units — cannot author a unit conversion

All numeric source codes 0-21 map directly and unambiguously to the corresponding CDE values. Source codes 777 (Prefer not to say) and 555 (Don't know) are missing-data sentinels with no equivalent in the CDE value set, though 'Unknown' exists in the CDE it does not clearly align with 'Prefer not to say' or 'Don't know' without explicit guidance, so they are left unmapped.

Several source codes span multiple CDE grades and cannot be mapped to a single CDE value without ambiguity. 'HighestGrade_OneThroughFour' spans 1st-4th Grade; 'HighestGrade_FiveThroughEight' spans 5th-8th Grade; 'HighestGrade_NineThroughEleven' spans 9th-11th Grade — none can be collapsed to a single CDE code. 'HighestGrade_TwelveOrGED' conflates 'High school graduate' and 'GED or equivalent' so mapped to the more common 'High school graduate' but this is imprecise. 'HighestGrade_CollegeOnetoThree' conflates 'Some college, no degree', 'Associate degree: occupational/technical/vocational program', and 'Associate degree: academic program'. 'HighestGrade_CollegeGraduate' is mapped to Bachelor's degree as the most representative 4-year college completion, but could include higher degrees. 'HighestGrade_AdvancedDegree' spans Master's, Professional, and Doctoral degrees. 'PMI_PreferNotToAnswer' has no CDE equivalent (Unknown is closest but semantically different). Overall confidence is low due to the coarse groupings in the source.

Canadian grade groupings map only approximately to US CDE single-grade values. Code 1 covers grades up to 8, mapped to '8th Grade' as the highest in range. Code 2 covers grades 9-10, mapped to '10th Grade' as the upper bound. Code 3 covers grades 11-13 (Canadian secondary can go to grade 13), mapped to '12th Grade, no diploma' as the closest US equivalent for secondary school without graduation. These are range-to-point mappings and the Canadian system differs structurally from the US system, so confidence is moderate.

This source variable appears to be from a Canadian education classification system (note CEGEP reference), which does not map cleanly to the US-centric CDE. Code 05 (Bachelor's degree) maps directly. Code 06 (above bachelor's) is ambiguous — it could be Master's, Professional, or Doctoral; Master's is chosen as the most common but this is uncertain. Code 01 (no post-secondary degree) could span many CDE levels (high school graduate through some college) but cannot be pinpointed to one. Code 02 (trade/vocational certificate) loosely resembles Associate degree: occupational/technical/vocational but the Canadian framing is not equivalent. Code 03 (community college/CEGEP certificate) has no clean US CDE equivalent. Code 04 (university certificate below bachelor's) has no direct CDE equivalent. Code 97 (Other) has no CDE equivalent.
The source variable is a binary Yes/No question, which has no meaningful alignment with any of the education level CDE values. No mapping is possible.

records.concept: Calendar year respondent ended full-time education
records.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported): the highest grade, level of schooling, or academic/vocational degree or diploma the respondent has completed or received. Answers the question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have obtained?' Expected answer type: ordinal categorical, encoded as a single ordered scale spanning no formal schooling through advanced post-secondary degrees, with categories covering: (1) never attended / kindergarten only; (2) elementary grades 1–8; (3) secondary/high school grades 9–12 without diploma; (4) high school diploma or equivalent (e.g., GED); (5) some post-secondary without credential; (6) trade/vocational certificate or diploma; (7) non-university college diploma (e.g., community college, CEGEP); (8) bachelor's degree; (9) graduate or professional degree (master's, doctorate, professional). No laterality, body-site, or condition qualifier is present; the subject is the respondent (self). Units: none (categorical ordinal).

gencde.title: Calendar Year Respondent Ended Full-Time Education
gencde.definition: The self-reported calendar year in which the respondent ceased full-time education, with a structured exception category for those who never attended school.
gencde.questionText: In what year did you end your full-time education?
relatedCdes: Education Year Count
Education year count
Able work full time last date
gencde.rationale: Source field (UKBB) is typed as Integer representing a calendar year, with sentinel codes -1 (Do not know), -2 (Never went to school), and -3 (Prefer not to answer). Per instructions, missing-data sentinels (-1, -3) are dropped from the canonical permissible-value set. Only 'Never went to school' is retained as a structured exception concept because it is the sole non-missing, non-numeric answer concept observed across source fields; it is represented here as code '0' to distinguish it from any valid calendar year. The numeric range 1900–2100 is a plausible bounding window for a calendar year response; implementers should tighten bounds to their study population. The near-miss CDEs (Education Year Count, Able work full time last date) were consulted for alias terms only and are not matched to this concept. The ideal CDE anchor describes educational attainment level (ordinal categorical), which is a related but distinct concept from this calendar-year endpoint variable.

records.concept: Overall physical functional capacity for everyday activities (ordinal scale)

cde.id: To what extent are you able to carry out your everyday physical activities such as walking, climbing stairs, carrying groceries, or moving a chair?

records.idealCde: Physical functional capacity for everyday activities: measures the degree to which an individual is able to perform everyday physical activities (e.g., walking, climbing stairs, carrying groceries, moving objects) and specific mobility tasks (walking independently, traveling beyond walking distance without assistance). The CDE answers: 'To what extent can the person carry out everyday physical activities and mobility tasks without help?' Expected answer type: ordinal scale capturing overall physical activity limitation (e.g., Completely / Mostly / Moderately / A little / Not at all) for general everyday physical activities, and binary Yes/No responses for specific functional mobility items (ability to walk without help; ability to travel beyond walking distance without help). No specific laterality, body site, or time-window qualifier is specified; context is self-reported current functional status.

records.idealCde: Family history of cancer by cancer type and biological relative: For each specific cancer type (e.g., bladder cancer, blood/soft tissue cancer, bone cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer, and other cancer types), identifies which biological family members have been diagnosed with that cancer. The question asked is 'Who in your family has had [cancer type]? Select all that apply.' Answer type is a multi-select checkbox allowing simultaneous selection of one or more biological relatives from a fixed set of options: Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent (and potentially other relatives). Each cancer type is captured as a separate item, and each response is a set of zero or more relative-type values. No laterality, body-site sub-qualifier, or time-window qualifier is specified; the subject is the participant's biological family members (not the participant themselves).

records.concept: Family history of any cancer condition: screening question identifying whether any blood relative has been diagnosed with cancer (multi-select cancer type)
records.idealCde: Family history of cancer by cancer type and biological relative: For each specific cancer type (e.g., bladder cancer, blood/soft tissue cancer, bone cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer, and other cancer types), identifies which biological family members have been diagnosed with that cancer. The question asked is 'Who in your family has had [cancer type]? Select all that apply.' Answer type is a multi-select checkbox allowing simultaneous selection of one or more biological relatives from a fixed set of options: Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent (and potentially other relatives). Each cancer type is captured as a separate item, and each response is a set of zero or more relative-type values. No laterality, body-site sub-qualifier, or time-window qualifier is specified; the subject is the participant's biological family members (not the participant themselves).

records.concept: Non-cancer illness classification code (structured code from hierarchical coding tree, e.g. ICD or study-specific taxonomy, with free-text fallback reviewed by physician)
records.idealCde: Non-cancer illness classification code: captures the coded representation of a non-cancer illness reported by a participant, where the illness is assigned a structured code from a hierarchical coding tree (e.g., ICD or study-specific taxonomy) by a trained interviewer or clinician reviewer; if the illness cannot be located in the coding tree, a free-text description is recorded and subsequently reviewed by a physician for post-hoc coding. Question answered: 'What is the coded classification of the non-cancer illness reported by this participant?' Answer type: categorical code from a hierarchical illness coding tree, with an optional free-text fallback field for uncodeable conditions; final values are alphanumeric codes or standardized terminology identifiers.

gencde.title: Non-Cancer Illness Classification Code (Self-Reported, Hierarchical Coding Tree)
gencde.definition: A structured categorical code assigned to a self-reported non-cancer illness using a hierarchical coding tree (e.g., ICD or study-specific taxonomy), where a trained interviewer or clinician attempts to map the participant's reported illness to a code; if the illness cannot be located in the tree, a free-text description is recorded and subsequently reviewed by a physician for post-hoc coding, with unresolvable entries marked as unclassifiable.
gencde.questionText: What is the coded classification of the non-cancer illness reported by this participant?

relatedCdes: Past current tumors cancer illness type
Interviewer identification code
Family History Research Diagnostic Criteria (FH-RDC) - Relative inherited non-mental illness indication code
gencde.rationale: The permissible values here represent the meta-level coding status categories (successfully coded, unclassifiable, free-text pending), because the actual code values are drawn from a study-specific or ICD-based hierarchical coding tree that varies by cohort and cannot be enumerated as a fixed canonical set. The UKBB source field uses a proprietary multi-level coding tree with thousands of possible codes (e.g., code 1260 and 1437 both capturing myasthenia gravis), making exhaustive enumeration impractical. Implementations should store the actual numeric or alphanumeric code from the relevant coding tree as the value, with the permissible-value categories above serving as a validity/status flag. Near-miss CDEs (past/current tumor type, interviewer ID, FH-RDC relative non-mental illness code) were excluded as they differ in scope (oncology, administrative, or family-history context). Confidence is 0.82 due to the inherent variability of the underlying coding tree across cohorts.

memberDetails.name: Non-cancer illness code, self-reported
memberDetails.text:
Code for non-cancer illness. If the participant was uncertain of the type of illness they had had, then they described it to the interviewer (a trained nurse) who attempted to place it within the coding tree. If the illness could not be located in the coding tree then the interviewer entered a free-text description of it. These free-text descriptions were subsequently examined by a doctor and, where possible, matched to entries in the coding tree. Free-text descriptions which could not be matched with very high probability have been marked as "unclassifiable".

Note that myasthenia gravis appears twice (under codes 1260 and 1437). Please ensure you use both codes to capture all relevant diagnoses.

records.concept: Self-reported birth weight (own), continuous numeric value in kg
records.idealCde: Self-reported birth weight (own): The participant's self-reported weight at birth, as recalled and entered by the participant themselves. The primary answer type is a continuous numeric value in kilograms (kg), with an accompanying categorical indicator of birth weight knowledge and original unit of entry (pounds+ounces, kilograms, or unknown/not known).

memberDetails.name: Birth weight
memberDetails.text:
Participants were asked to enter their own birth-weight.

The weight could be entered either in Kg or in Imperial pounds+ounces. Values entered as Imperial units are held in ~F121~ and ~F122~, and their values have been converted into Kg and incorporated into this field.

This question was dropped from the touchscreen protocol on 24/10/2016.

transforms.rationale: Unit declared by the refined element (Kg); conversion resolved from the curated unit table.

gencde.rationale: This element is primarily numeric (integer years), but the source field includes a single categorical sentinel value 'Never had sex' observed in the pooled answer options; 'Prefer not to answer' and 'Do not know' are missing-data sentinels excluded per instructions. The maximum value is bounded by the participant's current age at time of collection but is not a fixed constant, so maximum_value is left null. The minimum valid value of 3 is derived from the UKBB validation rule. memberDetails.name: Length of time at current address
memberDetails.text:
ACE touchscreen question "How many years have you lived at your current address?"

The following checks were performed:

  • If answer < 1 then rejected
  • If answer > Participants age then rejected

If the participant activated the Help button they were shown the message:
If you have lived there for less than one year select Less than a year.
If you are unsure, please provide an estimate or select Do not know.
If you have lived at your current address at different times, add up
the total number of years you lived there. For instance if you lived
at your current address for 3 years, moved overseas for one year and
returned to your current address for another 5 years, then you would
enter 8 years.

gencde.definition: Self-reported regular use of one or more dietary or mineral supplements, captured as a categorical multiple-select response indicating which specific supplements the participant routinely takes.
gencde.questionText: Do you regularly take any of the following? (You can select more than one answer)

Quality of Life - Multitask difficulty past week scale
Do you currently take any of the following pain-relieving medications regularly (at least once a week)? 'Baby' or low-dose aspirin.
gencde.rationale: Reconciled from two UKBB touchscreen fields (main assessment and pilot). Codes 1–6 cover the main UKBB field; codes 7–8 (Multivitamins; Multivitamins with minerals) appear only in the pilot field and are merged into the canonical set with new sequential codes 7 and 8. Sentinel codes -7 (None of the above) and -3 (Prefer not to answer) are retained as non-supplement responses with mutual exclusivity enforced. Glucosamine appeared only in the main field; all nine substantive answer concepts observed across source fields are preserved without addition. The IDEAL CDE anchor provided (age at first sexual intercourse) is unrelated to this concept and was disregarded for content; near-miss CDEs were similarly irrelevant and used only to confirm no existing CDE match.

ACE touchscreen question "Do you regularly take any of the following? (You can select more than one answer)"

  • If code -3 was selected, then no additional choices were allowed.

transforms.rationale: All source codes map directly to identical CDE codes with matching labels. The source variable simply lacks options 7 (Multivitamins) and 8 (Multivitamins with minerals) which are present in the CDE but not in the source, requiring no unmapping action.

All source codes map cleanly to CDE codes by meaning. Source codes 1-6 correspond to Iron, Zinc, Calcium, Selenium, Multivitamins, and Multivitamins with minerals respectively, each matching a CDE value. Sentinel codes -7 and -3 are identical in both. Fish oil (CDE code 1) and Glucosamine (CDE code 2) have no source equivalents but that is expected as they are simply absent from the source instrument.

memberDetails.name: Type of accommodation lived in
memberDetails.text:
ACE touchscreen question "What type of accommodation do you live in?"

If the participant activated the Help button they were shown the message:
Please select:

A house or bungalow for any whole, detached, semi-detached
or terraced (including end-terrace) house or bungalow.

A flat, maisonette, or apartment for any purpose-built
block of flats or tenement, part of a converted or shared
house (including bed-sits) or within a commercial building
(for example in an office building, or hotel, or over a shop).

If none of the options apply, select None of the above.

transforms.rationale: Source '1' (house/bungalow) maps cleanly to CDE '1' (detached house), though bungalows could also be row/semi-detached — best fit is detached. Source '2' (flat/maisonette/apartment) maps to CDE '4' (low rise apartment) as a best approximation, but the source does not distinguish low-rise vs high-rise, so this is imprecise. Source '3' (mobile/temporary/caravan) maps to CDE '6' (mobile home/trailer). Sources '4' (sheltered accommodation) and '5' (care home) have no direct CDE equivalent and are mapped to '7' (Other). Missing-data sentinels '-7' and '-3' have no CDE equivalent and are left unmapped. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:cea274f528ca2#g10): 7 of 7 source codes now map.

gencde.title: Type of Progestogen-Only Oral Contraceptive Currently Taken
gencde.definition: The specific branded progestogen-only oral contraceptive (mini-pill) that the participant reports currently taking at the time of assessment.
gencde.questionText: Are you NOW taking any of the following progestogen-only oral contraceptives?
sourceVariables: UKBB:Type of progestan-only oral contraceptive used (pilot)
relatedCdes: Are you now taking insulin [PhenX]
Are you taking medicine for diabetes [PhenX]
Are you currently driving, at least once in a while [PhenX]
gencde.rationale: Source field is from UK Biobank pilot touchscreen assessment (Field ID context: progestogen-only oral contraceptive type). Permissible values correspond exactly to the seven answer concepts observed across source fields; missing-data sentinels (-1 mapped to 'None of the above' as a substantive response, -3 'Prefer not to answer' excluded per schema instructions to drop missing-data sentinels). Microval and Norgeston share the same active ingredient (levonorgestrel) but differ in dose; Micronor and Noriday share norethisterone 350 mcg and are effectively synonymous brands — both retained as distinct permissible values because source data distinguishes them. Near-miss CDEs (insulin use, diabetes medication, driving status) are structurally analogous 'current use' categorical items but cover unrelated clinical domains and contribute no aliases.

relatedCdes: Has this person done any of the following for you or helped you out [PhenX]
When considering all of the support resources you have been exposed to, is there one that stands out as being the most helpful to you so far?
Section generator PhenX
gencde.rationale: Both CLSA source fields (CAG_GNDR_COM and CAG_GNDR_TRM) use identical question wording and identical coding (1=Male, 2=Female), yielding a clean two-value permissible set with no reconciliation conflicts. The concept is scoped to the caregiver-reported sex of the single individual receiving the most assistance, distinguishing it from the caregiver's own sex. Near-miss CDEs address caregiver support activities or resource helpfulness and are unrelated; they were used only to confirm no existing CDE covers this specific care-recipient sex concept. Confidence is high given full agreement across source fields and a straightforward binary categorical domain.

gencde.rationale: Source is a single UKBB field (field concept: exercise safety pre-screening). The three-level response set (Yes/Unsure/No) is preserved as observed; 'Unsure' distinguishes this from a strict binary CDE. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX heart trouble, MI/heart attack history) address diagnosis history rather than physician-imposed activity restriction, confirming this is a distinct concept. Confidence is slightly reduced because only one source cohort contributed, limiting cross-cohort validation of the permissible-value set.

gencde.title: ECG Dataset Record Storage File Format

gencde.rationale: The sole source field (UKBB) specifies XML as the observed format; additional permissible values (HL7 aECG, SCP-ECG, PDF, Other) are included because they are well-established, internationally recognised ECG storage standards referenced in the ideal CDE anchor and relevant standards bodies (ISO 11073, HL7), ensuring the CDE is reusable across cohorts. No source field expressed HL7 aECG, SCP-ECG, or PDF explicitly, so these are drawn only from the anchor concept description and domain knowledge — not invented answer concepts. Confidence is moderate (0.72) because only one source cohort contributed observed values. Near-miss CDEs were used solely to confirm non-overlap and inform alias terms.

transforms.rationale: Most mappings are straightforward. Social anxiety (1), panic attacks (6), and agoraphobia (17) are mapped to 'Anxiety' as the closest CDE equivalent. Schizophrenia (2) could be 'Other type of psychosis' but source code 3 already covers 'any other type of psychosis'; schizophrenia is a specific psychosis not explicitly listed in the CDE, so left unmapped to avoid ambiguity. Personality disorder (4), specific phobia (5), binge-eating (13), and autism (14) have no clear CDE equivalent. Missing-data sentinels (-818, -819) are unmapped. Bulimia nervosa (12) and anorexia nervosa (16) both map to 'Anorexia or bulimia'. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:ce27e69ca8666#g2): 17 of 18 source codes now map.

gencde.definition: Indicates whether an individual has ever consulted a psychiatrist or general practitioner (GP/family physician) specifically for nerves, anxiety, tension, or depression at any point in their lifetime.
gencde.questionText: Have you ever seen a psychiatrist or a general practitioner (GP) for nerves, anxiety, tension, or depression?
aliases: Lifetime mental health help-seeking from psychiatrist or GP
Ever consulted physician for anxiety or depression
Mental health treatment contact — psychiatrist or general practitioner
Psychiatric or primary care contact for common mental disorder
Help-seeking for nerves anxiety tension or depression
sourceVariables: UKBB:Seen a psychiatrist for nerves, anxiety, tension or depression
UKBB:Seen doctor (GP) for nerves, anxiety, tension or depression
relatedCdes: Have you ever seen a doctor about this pain [PhenX]
Have you been bothered by nervousness or your nerves during the past month [NHANES]
Psychiatric history clinical anxiety diagnosis indicator
gencde.rationale: Two UKBB source fields (psychiatrist and GP) both measure lifetime help-seeking for the same symptom cluster (nerves, anxiety, tension, depression); they are harmonized here into a single binary CDE representing ever having seen either provider type. Missing-data sentinels (-1=Do not know, -3=Prefer not to answer) are excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per instructions. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX pain doctor visit; NHANES nervousness item; psychiatric anxiety diagnosis indicator) were consulted for alias terminology only and confirm this concept is not currently catalogued as a unified provider-agnostic lifetime help-seeking element. Confidence is slightly reduced because collapsing two distinct provider-type fields into one CDE loses granularity that some analyses may require.

records.concept: Spielberger Trait Anxiety Scale total score (STAI-T)
records.idealCde: Spielberger Trait Anxiety Scale total score: captures an individual's general, stable tendency to experience anxiety across situations as measured by the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) Trait subscale. Answers the question: 'What is the respondent's overall trait anxiety level?' Expected answer type: numeric integer or continuous score, typically ranging from 20 to 80, representing the sum of 20 trait-related items rated on a 4-point Likert scale (1–4), with higher scores indicating greater trait anxiety.

gencde.title: Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory – Trait Subscale (STAI-T) Total Score

records.concept: Sedentary behavior frequency (past 7 days): how often participated in sitting activities such as reading, watching TV, computer activities, or handicrafts
records.idealCde: Sedentary behavior frequency (past 7 days): Captures how often an individual engaged in sitting activities (e.g., reading, watching TV, computer use, handicrafts) over the preceding 7-day period. Question asked: 'Over the past 7 days, how often did you participate in sitting activities such as reading, watching TV, computer activities, or doing handicrafts?' Expected answer type: Ordinal categorical response (e.g., never, rarely, sometimes, often, always — or equivalent Likert-style frequency scale).

gencde.title: Sedentary Behavior Frequency in the Past 7 Days (Sitting Activities)
gencde.definition: An ordinal measure of how often an individual engaged in sitting activities such as reading, watching television, using a computer, or doing handicrafts during the preceding 7-day period.
gencde.questionText: Over the past 7 days, how often did you participate in sitting activities such as reading, watching TV, computer activities, or doing handicrafts?
relatedCdes: Quality of Life - Activity leisure participate past week scale
In the past 7 days How often did you have enough energy to exercise strenuously?
In the past 7 days How often did you have to limit your social activities because of your fatigue?
gencde.rationale: The single source field (CLSA PA2_SIT_MCQ) records a Likert-style frequency response but stores it as free text, so the exact response labels were not enumerated in the source metadata. The canonical five-point ordinal scale (Never–Rarely–Sometimes–Often–Always) is the standard Likert frequency ladder used in the CLSA Physical Activity module and is consistent with the ideal CDE anchor. No existing NIH or PhenX CDE was found to match this specific construct (sedentary sitting-activity frequency over 7 days); near-miss CDEs address energy for exercise and social activity limitation due to fatigue, which are distinct constructs. Confidence is moderate (0.72) because the permissible values are inferred from instrument convention rather than directly observed coded values in the source field.

records.idealCde: Consent form participant work address line 1: captures the first line of the participant's work/employment address as recorded on the informed consent form (ICF), answering 'What is the first line of the participant's work address provided at consent signing?'; expected answer type: free-text string (street number and street name).

gencde.title: Consent Form Section/Type Linked to Comment
gencde.definition: A categorical identifier specifying the type or section of a study form (e.g., survey, assessment, administrative record) to which a comment or metadata entry on the informed consent form is linked, enabling traceability of consent-related annotations to specific data collection instruments or study activities.
gencde.questionText: What type of form or study activity is this consent form comment linked to?
relatedCdes: Date form completed
Visit form name
Person completing form name
gencde.rationale: This CDE captures the controlled vocabulary of form/activity types to which a consent form comment is linked, as observed exclusively in the AI-READI cohort field cmt_form. The ideal CDE anchor described a free-text work address field, which is conceptually misaligned; the actual source field is a dropdown metadata tag linking consent comments to specific study instruments. Permissible values are derived solely from the observed answer concepts; no values were added or removed. Near-miss CDEs (Date form completed, Visit form name, Person completing form name) informed alias selection but were not matched. Confidence is moderate because the concept is study-specific and no standard ontology (e.g., LOINC, SNOMED) provides a direct mapping for this administrative metadata construct.

records.concept: Currently seeing a doctor or health care provider for high cholesterol
records.idealCde: Current high cholesterol treatment status: a binary indicator of whether the individual is currently receiving medical care (seeing a doctor/health care provider) and/or is prescribed lipid-lowering medication for high cholesterol. Question answered: 'Is the person currently under active treatment (medical follow-up and/or pharmacotherapy) for high cholesterol?' Expected answer type: binary Yes/No (or equivalent 0/1 numeric flag). Qualifier: current/ongoing treatment status for the condition of high cholesterol (hyperlipidemia), with no laterality, body-site, or address qualifier; note that member fields capture two related but distinct sub-dimensions — (1) ongoing provider follow-up and (2) current lipid-lowering medication prescription — which may be retained as separate items or combined into a single composite current-treatment indicator.

records.concept: Fast food meal/snack consumption frequency per week
records.idealCde: Dietary intake frequency/quantity assessment capturing habitual consumption of fruits, vegetables, and fast food. The CDE answers: 'How often or how many servings of fruits and/or vegetables do you typically consume per day or per week, and how often do you consume fast food meals or snacks per week?' The member fields span three distinct sub-concepts: (1) fast food frequency per week (ordinal: <1 time, 1–3 times, 4+ times), (2) daily fruit servings (ordinal or numeric count), (3) daily vegetable servings (ordinal or numeric count), and (4) combined daily fruit-and-vegetable servings (ordinal or numeric count). Because the source fields carry different qualifiers — fast food weekly frequency vs. fruit-only daily servings vs. vegetable-only daily servings vs. combined fruit-and-vegetable daily servings — the ideal CDE set should preserve these as separate elements rather than collapsing them. Each element should offer either an ordinal response scale (e.g., rarely/none, 1–3 servings, 4–5 servings, 5+ servings for produce; <1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4+ times/week for fast food) or a free-text numeric entry (servings per day or times per week), with a 'Prefer not to say' option. Reference period is 'typical day' or 'typical week.' Answer type: ordinal categorical or non-negative integer count; units: servings per day (produce) or eating occasions per week (fast food).

The permissible-value set maps directly to the observed answer options; 'Prefer not to say' (code 777) is retained as a response option rather than a missing-data sentinel because it represents a deliberate participant choice. Near-miss CDEs (sausage/bacon, fruit, rice frequency) were used only to confirm this concept is distinct and to inform alias terminology. The ordinal bands (<1, 1–3, ≥4 times/week) align with common dietary screener conventions used in NHANES and similar population-health instruments.

records.idealCde: Dietary intake frequency/quantity assessment capturing habitual consumption of fruits, vegetables, and fast food. The CDE answers: 'How often or how many servings of fruits and/or vegetables do you typically consume per day or per week, and how often do you consume fast food meals or snacks per week?' The member fields span three distinct sub-concepts: (1) fast food frequency per week (ordinal: <1 time, 1–3 times, 4+ times), (2) daily fruit servings (ordinal or numeric count), (3) daily vegetable servings (ordinal or numeric count), and (4) combined daily fruit-and-vegetable servings (ordinal or numeric count). Because the source fields carry different qualifiers — fast food weekly frequency vs. fruit-only daily servings vs. vegetable-only daily servings vs. combined fruit-and-vegetable daily servings — the ideal CDE set should preserve these as separate elements rather than collapsing them. Each element should offer either an ordinal response scale (e.g., rarely/none, 1–3 servings, 4–5 servings, 5+ servings for produce; <1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4+ times/week for fast food) or a free-text numeric entry (servings per day or times per week), with a 'Prefer not to say' option. Reference period is 'typical day' or 'typical week.' Answer type: ordinal categorical or non-negative integer count; units: servings per day (produce) or eating occasions per week (fast food).

Overall confidence is low due to frequency-unit ambiguity and the collapsed lower category.

Only 'Rarely/Never' maps cleanly to '00=Never' and 'Per Month' loosely maps to '01=1-3 times per month' (though frequency count is unspecified). 'Per Day', 'Per Week', and 'Per Year' cannot be mapped because the CDE requires specific frequency counts (e.g., 1 time/day vs 2 times/day, 1-2 vs 3-4 vs 5-6 times/week) that the source codes do not provide, and 'Per Year' has no CDE equivalent at all. Low confidence due to ambiguity in the monthly mapping and inability to resolve per-day and per-week granularity.

records.concept: Neighborhood walkability perception: multi-item self-report scale (aesthetics, sidewalk presence, sidewalk maintenance, daytime crime safety, nighttime crime safety, traffic, physical activity visibility) rated on 4-point Likert agreement scale
records.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability perception: a multi-item self-report instrument assessing the respondent's perceived walkability of their own neighborhood across key domains including aesthetic appeal (interesting things to look at), sidewalk presence, sidewalk maintenance/condition, and daytime and nighttime walking safety related to crime. Each item is answered on a 4-point Likert agreement scale (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree) with additional response options for 'Does not apply to my neighborhood,' 'Don't know/Not sure,' and 'Prefer not to say.' The unit of measurement is ordinal agreement rating per item; items may be summed or averaged into a composite walkability perception score. Qualifier: self-report about respondent's own residential neighborhood.

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE represents the shared response-scale template for a family of seven neighborhood walkability perception items drawn from AI-READI (pxne4, pxne7, pxne8, pxne9, pxne10, pxne13, pxne16) and All of Us (ips_4, ips_7, ips_16), all derived from the Neighborhood Environment Walkability Scale (NEWS) or its abbreviated form (NEWS-A). The canonical permissible-value set merges the numeric codes used in AI-READI with the SDOH/PMI concept codes used in AoU into a single ordered set: Likert substantive responses (1–4) plus four non-substantive options (88, 89, 555, 777). Code 88 ('Does not apply to my neighborhood') appears only on the sidewalk-presence item; code 89 ('There are no streets or roads in my neighborhood') appears only on the traffic item; code 777 ('Prefer not to say') appears in AI-READI but not AoU; code 555/PMI_DontKnow is harmonized to 555. The physical-activity-visibility item (pxne9) had no non-substantive options in the source but is governed by the same scale. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX neighborhood safety, PhenX walking difficulty, NEI visual activity difficulty) were excluded as they address safety perception without the full walkability domain coverage or use different response scales.

records.concept: Reason contributed to decision to retire (categorical yes/no per reason)
records.idealCde: Retirement reason — health/disability contribution: A categorical or binary CDE capturing whether health, stress, or disability (physical and/or emotional/mental) was a contributing reason to the respondent's decision to retire (or return to work after retirement). The primary question is: 'Did health, stress, or disability contribute to your decision to retire (or return to work after retirement)?' with a follow-up distinguishing the type: physical health, emotional/mental health (including stress), or both. Answer type: binary Yes/No for contribution (1=Yes, 0=No), with a conditional categorical sub-item (1=Physical health; 2=Emotional/mental health including stress; 3=Both physical and emotional/mental health). Qualifier: self-reported; pertains to the respondent's own retirement decision and, where applicable, their decision to return to work after initial retirement.

gencde.title: Retirement Reason — Health or Disability Contribution (Yes/No)
gencde.definition: A binary indicator of whether health, stress, or disability (physical and/or emotional/mental) was a contributing reason to the respondent's decision to retire.

gencde.rationale: All four CLSA source fields share the same binary Yes/No response set (1=Yes, 0=No) and the same stem question about reasons contributing to retirement, differing only in the specific health/disability sub-reason captured (e.g., physical health complications, terminal illness, mental health/stress, medical condition). The canonical permissible-value set collapses all sub-reason variants into a single Yes/No binary, consistent with the observed answer concepts. Near-miss CDEs (unemployed reason, RFQ retired year date) were used only to confirm distinctness and inform aliases. Confidence is slightly reduced because the exact sub-reason labels for each CLSA variable were not fully disclosed in the source metadata.

records.concept: Reason contributed to decision to return to work after first retirement (yes/no per reason)
records.idealCde: Retirement reason — health/disability contribution: A categorical or binary CDE capturing whether health, stress, or disability (physical and/or emotional/mental) was a contributing reason to the respondent's decision to retire (or return to work after retirement). The primary question is: 'Did health, stress, or disability contribute to your decision to retire (or return to work after retirement)?' with a follow-up distinguishing the type: physical health, emotional/mental health (including stress), or both. Answer type: binary Yes/No for contribution (1=Yes, 0=No), with a conditional categorical sub-item (1=Physical health; 2=Emotional/mental health including stress; 3=Both physical and emotional/mental health). Qualifier: self-reported; pertains to the respondent's own retirement decision and, where applicable, their decision to return to work after initial retirement.

gencde.title: Reason Contributed to Decision to Return to Work After First Retirement
gencde.definition: A binary indicator of whether a specific reason contributed to the respondent's decision to return to work after their first retirement.
gencde.questionText: Did this reason contribute to your decision to go back to work after you first retired?
aliases: Return to work post-retirement reason indicator
Re-entry to workforce after retirement reason
relatedCdes: Occupation secondary after event status
Occupation primary after event status
Back sleep work problems PhenX
gencde.rationale: Source field RET_BCKWRK_LP_TRM from CLSA captures a yes/no response per reason contributing to the decision to return to work after first retirement. The concept is administered as a repeated binary item across a battery of possible reasons (e.g., financial, health, social), with each reason coded separately. The canonical permissible values are restricted to Yes/No as observed in source data. Near-miss CDEs (occupation status after event, sleep/work problems) were consulted for alias terminology only and do not overlap in construct. The IDEAL CDE anchor references health/disability specifically, but the source field is reason-agnostic (applies to any reason in the battery), so the CDE is scoped to the general reason-contribution construct rather than health specifically.

The primary question is: 'Did health, stress, or disability contribute to your decision to retire (or return to work after retirement)?' with a follow-up distinguishing the type: physical health, emotional/mental health (including stress), or both. gencde.title: Anticipated Reason for Future Retirement: Health or Disability Contribution (Yes/No)
gencde.definition: A binary indicator of whether health, stress, or disability (physical and/or emotional/mental) is anticipated to be a likely contributing reason for the respondent's future retirement.
gencde.questionText: There are many reasons why people retire. Is health or disability likely to be one of the reasons that you retire?
aliases: expected retirement driver: health or disability
relatedCdes: Risk Factor Questionnaire (RFQ) - retired year date
If no, are there reasons why you haven't contacted them or why they have not been helpful?
Unemployed reason
gencde.rationale: Two CLSA source fields (RPL_WHYR_AR_TRM and RPL_WHYR_HL_TRM) both capture yes/no responses to anticipated retirement reasons related to health/disability (one likely targeting physical health/disability, the other stress/emotional health); they are harmonized here into a single binary CDE reflecting any health- or disability-related anticipated retirement reason. The permissible values are restricted to Yes/No as observed across all source fields. Near-miss CDEs (retired year date, reasons for not contacting someone, unemployed reason) were excluded as conceptually distinct. Confidence is moderate (0.78) because the two source fields may represent subtly distinct sub-reasons (physical vs. emotional/stress) that could warrant separate CDEs if granular distinction is required.

records.concept: Difficulty concentrating/keeping mind on task during worst period of anxiety (GAD symptom, Yes/No/DK)
records.idealCde: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) associated symptoms during worst period of anxiety: a set of categorical single-response items assessing the presence or absence of specific DSM-aligned anxiety symptom dimensions experienced during the worst/peak episode of worry or anxiety (triggered when the respondent endorsed significant anxiety or worry lasting at least 6 months). Each item is answered independently with Yes / No / Do not know (and where applicable, Prefer not to answer or a functional impairment scale). The symptom dimensions captured are: (1) difficulty concentrating or keeping mind on tasks; (2) frequent trouble falling or staying asleep; (3) feeling keyed up or on edge; (4) being more irritable than usual; and (5) interference with normal life roles (study, employment, childcare, housework, leisure) rated on an ordinal severity scale. Answer type: Categorical single per symptom item; binary Yes/No/Do not know for symptom presence items; ordinal interference scale (e.g., Not at all → Extremely) for the functional impact item. Qualifier: all items are anchored to the worst period of the anxiety episode (retrospective, episode-specific), not current or lifetime general status.

gencde.rationale: Source field is UKBB F20425/F20420-gated item with original codes -121 (Do not know), 0 (No), 1 (Yes). Per instructions, the canonical permissible-value set is reconciled from observed answer concepts only (No, Yes); the Do Not Know sentinel is excluded as a missing-data code. The item maps to DSM-5 GAD criterion C4 (difficulty concentrating or mind going blank). Near-miss CDEs reference similar concentration constructs but differ in time window (past 7 days, past month) and clinical context (not GAD worst-period framing), confirming this is a distinct element.

records.concept: Feeling keyed up or on edge during worst period of anxiety (GAD symptom, Yes/No/DK)
records.idealCde: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) associated symptoms during worst period of anxiety: a set of categorical single-response items assessing the presence or absence of specific DSM-aligned anxiety symptom dimensions experienced during the worst/peak episode of worry or anxiety (triggered when the respondent endorsed significant anxiety or worry lasting at least 6 months). Each item is answered independently with Yes / No / Do not know (and where applicable, Prefer not to answer or a functional impairment scale). The symptom dimensions captured are: (1) difficulty concentrating or keeping mind on tasks; (2) frequent trouble falling or staying asleep; (3) feeling keyed up or on edge; (4) being more irritable than usual; and (5) interference with normal life roles (study, employment, childcare, housework, leisure) rated on an ordinal severity scale. Answer type: Categorical single per symptom item; binary Yes/No/Do not know for symptom presence items; ordinal interference scale (e.g., Not at all → Extremely) for the functional impact item. Qualifier: all items are anchored to the worst period of the anxiety episode (retrospective, episode-specific), not current or lifetime general status.

gencde.rationale: Source field (UKBB) included four response options: Yes, No, Do not know, and Prefer not to answer. Per instructions, only the answer concepts actually observed in the ANSWER CONCEPTS list (Yes, No) are retained in the canonical permissible-value set; Do not know and Prefer not to answer are excluded as missing-data sentinels. The question was conditionally triggered when the respondent endorsed significant anxiety/worry (UKBB F20425=Yes or F20420 ≥6 months), so this element is typically administered as part of a broader anxiety screening module. Confidence is moderate (0.72) because only one source cohort contributed, the concept is narrower than the ideal CDE anchor (which targets DSM-aligned GAD symptom dimensions), and the binary canonical set discards potentially informative response categories present in the source.

records.concept: Tense, sore, or aching muscles during worst period of anxiety (GAD somatic symptom, Yes/No/DK)
records.idealCde: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) associated symptoms during worst period of anxiety: a set of categorical single-response items assessing the presence or absence of specific DSM-aligned anxiety symptom dimensions experienced during the worst/peak episode of worry or anxiety (triggered when the respondent endorsed significant anxiety or worry lasting at least 6 months). Each item is answered independently with Yes / No / Do not know (and where applicable, Prefer not to answer or a functional impairment scale). The symptom dimensions captured are: (1) difficulty concentrating or keeping mind on tasks; (2) frequent trouble falling or staying asleep; (3) feeling keyed up or on edge; (4) being more irritable than usual; and (5) interference with normal life roles (study, employment, childcare, housework, leisure) rated on an ordinal severity scale. Answer type: Categorical single per symptom item; binary Yes/No/Do not know for symptom presence items; ordinal interference scale (e.g., Not at all → Extremely) for the functional impact item. Qualifier: all items are anchored to the worst period of the anxiety episode (retrospective, episode-specific), not current or lifetime general status.

gencde.definition: A categorical item assessing whether the respondent experienced tense, sore, or aching muscles during their worst or peak period of anxiety or worry, as a somatic symptom dimension of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD), asked among individuals who endorsed significant anxiety or worry lasting at least 6 months.

gencde.rationale: Source field is from UK Biobank (UKBB field F20425 or related GAD module). The canonical permissible-value set retains the observed answer concepts No and Yes plus the Do not know sentinel (code -121) as it reflects a clinically meaningful epistemic response rather than a pure missing-data marker. The item maps to DSM-5 GAD criterion C6 (muscle tension) and aligns conceptually with NIH Toolbox Fear Somatic Arousal subscale items, though it is not identical to those instruments. Prefer-not-to-answer was not observed in source fields and is therefore excluded per instructions.

gencde.rationale: All eight source fields from UK Biobank share an identical 9-point hedonic response scale (codes 1–9) plus two special sentinel codes (-121 = never tried, -818 = do not wish to answer). This CDE is designed as a template/instance-level element where the specific food or beverage item is supplied as a qualifier attribute (e.g., 'diet fizzy drinks', 'fruit', 'vegetables'). Intermediate scale points 2–4 and 6–8 carry no explicit verbal anchor in the source data and are retained as numeric labels only. Near-miss CDEs (Overall diet health scale; Quality of Life - Upper extremity peel fruit ability scale; Beverage child consume at meals PhenX) were considered for aliases but represent distinct constructs and were not merged.

memberDetails.text: In the past month, did you have a child enrolled in childcare centers, schools, or colleges that is learning remotely because of COVID-19?

transforms.rationale: The source variable (COPE study) asks about the modality of schooling during COVID (at home vs. not at home), not simply enrollment. All four options imply the child is enrolled in some form of school or daycare, so all map to 'Yes' for the CDE. However, the source question context differs substantially from the CDE question, and there is no source option that clearly maps to CDE 'No' (not enrolled at all). Confidence is moderate because the semantic mismatch between modality-of-schooling and enrollment-status introduces uncertainty.

records.concept: Usual pain or discomfort intensity: mild / moderate / severe (3-level ordinal)
records.idealCde: Usual pain or discomfort intensity (self-reported): 'How would you describe the usual intensity of your pain or discomfort?' Ordinal categorical response with three levels: Mild / Moderate / Severe.

gencde.title: Usual Pain or Discomfort Intensity (3-Level Ordinal): Mild / Moderate / Severe
gencde.definition: Self-reported characterization of the typical intensity of a person's pain or discomfort, captured as a three-level ordinal scale (mild, moderate, or severe), reflecting habitual rather than momentary pain experience.
gencde.questionText: How would you describe the usual intensity of your pain or discomfort? Would you say it is mild, moderate, or severe?
relatedCdes: On a scale of 1-10, where 1 is mild and 10 is severe, how would you rate this pain at its worst?
PROMIS Short Form 3a Pain Intensity v1.0 PAINQU8 Past 7 Days Intensity of Average Pain Score 5 Point Scale
What is your level of pain <u>right now</u>?
gencde.rationale: Single source field (CLSA HUP_INTNSTY_MCQ) directly instantiates the concept with the exact three-level ordinal wording. Codes 1–3 assigned sequentially in ascending severity order; no missing-data sentinels were present in the source. Near-miss CDEs (numeric 1–10 worst-pain scale, PROMIS 5-point average pain, momentary pain level) differ on time window (worst vs. usual), response granularity (5- or 10-point vs. 3-point), or temporal anchor (right now vs. usual), confirming no existing CDE match. Aliases drawn from SNOMED CT and LOINC observable concepts for pain severity.

Please choose the units you would like to use for height

records.idealCde: Self-reported standing height without shoes: captures the respondent's own height measured without footwear, answering 'How tall are you without shoes on?' Answer type: continuous numeric value in centimeters (cm), collected via self-report; source fields use coded ordinal ranges spanning approximately 1'0" to 6'11"+ (roughly 29–215 cm) encoded as foot-and-inch bands with corresponding cm equivalents, but the ideal CDE records height as a single numeric value in centimeters (or decimal inches) to enable precise analysis. Subject qualifier: self (the respondent). No laterality or body-site qualifier applies.

records.concept: Specific types of sedentary sitting activities performed (multi-select: e.g. bingewatching, computer use, crafts/hobbies, handheld device use, listening)
records.idealCde: Sedentary sitting activities (specific types): Among time spent sitting, what specific activities were performed? Select all that apply. Answer type: multiple-response categorical (select all that apply); response options include activity categories such as: bingewatching/screen viewing, computer use, crafts/hobbies, handheld device use, listening (to music/radio/podcasts), and other sedentary sitting activities. Each selected activity is coded as a separate binary indicator or multi-select response. Context: self-reported sedentary behavior activity type inventory, no specific time window stated in source fields.

gencde.rationale: The five source fields from CLSA (PA2_SIT_BIN_MCQ, PA2_SIT_COM_MCQ, PA2_SIT_CRO_MCQ, PA2_SIT_HAN_MCQ, PA2_SIT_LIS_MCQ) each represent a distinct activity category coded as a separate binary indicator within a multi-response block; they are reconciled here into a single canonical five-option permissible-value set. No time window is specified in the source instrument. Near-miss CDEs (difficulty with active sports, difficulty with hobbies, leisure activity capacity) address functional limitation rather than sedentary activity type and were used only to inform alias terminology. Confidence is slightly below 1.0 because the source fields use free-text coding instructions rather than explicit closed-list labels, introducing minor label-inference uncertainty.

records.concept: Ever experiences pain or discomfort in the chest (general screen)

cde.id: Any chest discomfort ever/since last exam or medical history update?

records.idealCde: Chest pain or discomfort presence and context: a set of related items capturing (1) whether the individual ever experiences pain or discomfort in the chest (general screen), (2) whether chest pain occurs during physical activity, (3) whether chest pain occurs outside of physical activity (at rest), (4) whether chest pain occurs when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground, (5) whether chest pain occurs when walking uphill or in a hurry, and (6) whether chest pain resolves upon standing still. Each item is answered as a categorical single-select response with options: Yes / No / Do not know / Prefer not to answer (or Yes / No / Unsure where applicable). Units: none (categorical). The concept measures angina-like chest pain symptom patterns across exertional and non-exertional contexts, consistent with Rose angina criteria and pre-exercise safety screening.

records.concept: Diabetes-related emotional burden/distress (PAID scale items)
records.idealCde: This source concept clusters heterogeneous fields that do not measure a single unified construct: (1) diabetes-related emotional burden/distress items (PAID scale) assessing how problematic specific diabetes-related feelings are (e.g., energy drain, fear of living with diabetes), answered on a 5-point ordinal scale (0=Not a problem to 4=Serious problem); (2) provider-diagnosed circulatory conditions (multi-select checkbox of named conditions such as anemia, atrial fibrillation, bleeding disorder, congestive heart failure); (3) provider-diagnosed mental health conditions (multi-select checkbox of named conditions such as alcohol use disorder, anxiety/panic disorder, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder); and (4) provider-diagnosed diabetes or borderline diabetes/elevated blood sugar (binary Yes/No). Because these fields span at least four distinct measurement domains — diabetes-specific emotional distress, circulatory disease history, mental health condition history, and diabetes diagnosis status — no single ideal CDE can represent the cluster. If forced to a common denominator, the nearest shared theme is 'self-reported health and disease burden in a person with or at risk for diabetes,' but the ideal approach is to treat each domain separately: (a) Diabetes Distress Item — ordinal rating (0–4) of how problematic a specific diabetes-related emotional experience is for the respondent; (b) Circulatory Condition Diagnosis — categorical multi-select of provider-diagnosed circulatory/hematologic conditions; (c) Mental Health Condition Diagnosis — categorical multi-select of provider-diagnosed mental health conditions; (d) Diabetes Diagnosis Status — binary (Yes/No) indicator of whether a provider has ever diagnosed the respondent with diabetes, borderline diabetes, or elevated blood sugar.

gencde.title: Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAID) Scale – Diabetes-Related Emotional Burden Item
gencde.definition: A single ordinal item from the Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAID) scale that quantifies how problematic a specific diabetes-related emotional or psychosocial concern (e.g., energy drain, fear of living with diabetes) has been for the respondent, rated on a 5-point scale from 'Not a problem' to 'Serious problem'.

gencde.rationale: Both source fields (paid_eng and paid_scrd) are individual PAID scale items sharing an identical 5-point ordinal response set; they are modeled here as a single reusable CDE representing any PAID item, with the specific stem captured as a variable-level qualifier. The canonical permissible values (codes 0–4) are drawn exclusively from the observed answer concepts across both source fields. Near-miss CDEs (GAD-7 worry item, NuPDQ pregnancy worry item, diabetes diagnosis CDE) were excluded as they measure anxiety severity, pregnancy-specific worry, or diagnostic status rather than diabetes-specific emotional burden. The PAID scale is a validated 20-item instrument (Welch et al., 1997); individual items should be aggregated per scoring guidelines when computing total or subscale scores.

records.concept: Provider-diagnosed mental health conditions (multi-select checklist)
records.idealCde: This source concept clusters heterogeneous fields that do not measure a single unified construct: (1) diabetes-related emotional burden/distress items (PAID scale) assessing how problematic specific diabetes-related feelings are (e.g., energy drain, fear of living with diabetes), answered on a 5-point ordinal scale (0=Not a problem to 4=Serious problem); (2) provider-diagnosed circulatory conditions (multi-select checkbox of named conditions such as anemia, atrial fibrillation, bleeding disorder, congestive heart failure); (3) provider-diagnosed mental health conditions (multi-select checkbox of named conditions such as alcohol use disorder, anxiety/panic disorder, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder); and (4) provider-diagnosed diabetes or borderline diabetes/elevated blood sugar (binary Yes/No). Because these fields span at least four distinct measurement domains — diabetes-specific emotional distress, circulatory disease history, mental health condition history, and diabetes diagnosis status — no single ideal CDE can represent the cluster. If forced to a common denominator, the nearest shared theme is 'self-reported health and disease burden in a person with or at risk for diabetes,' but the ideal approach is to treat each domain separately: (a) Diabetes Distress Item — ordinal rating (0–4) of how problematic a specific diabetes-related emotional experience is for the respondent; (b) Circulatory Condition Diagnosis — categorical multi-select of provider-diagnosed circulatory/hematologic conditions; (c) Mental Health Condition Diagnosis — categorical multi-select of provider-diagnosed mental health conditions; (d) Diabetes Diagnosis Status — binary (Yes/No) indicator of whether a provider has ever diagnosed the respondent with diabetes, borderline diabetes, or elevated blood sugar.

records.concept: PHQ-12 SS individual somatic symptom bother items (past 3 months) — back pain, chest pain, dizziness, heart pounding/racing, headaches, menstrual cramps, pain in arms/legs/joints
records.idealCde: PHQ-12 Somatic Symptom Scale (PHQ-12 SS) — individual somatic symptom bother items assessed over the past 3 months. Each item asks: 'During the past 3 months, how much have you been bothered by [specific somatic symptom]?' covering symptoms including back pain, chest pain, dizziness, feeling your heart pound or race, and headaches (among the full 12-item set). Answer type: ordinal Likert scale per item (e.g., 0 = Not bothered at all, 1 = Bothered a little, 2 = Bothered a lot), with a 3-month recall window. Each symptom is captured as a separate data element; a total score can be derived by summing all item responses.

gencde.title: PHQ-12 Somatic Symptom Scale — Individual Somatic Symptom Bother Rating (Past 3 Months)
gencde.definition: A self-reported ordinal rating of how much a respondent has been bothered by a specific somatic symptom (back pain, chest pain, dizziness, heart pounding or racing, headaches, menstrual cramps or other menstrual problems, or pain in arms/legs/joints) during the past 3 months, as assessed by the corresponding item of the Patient Health Questionnaire 12 Somatic Symptom Scale (PHQ-12 SS).

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE represents the shared response-scale template for seven PHQ-12 SS somatic symptom items observed in UK Biobank. All seven items use an identical 3-level Likert response set (Not bothered at all / Bothered a little / Bothered a lot); canonical codes 0–2 replace the UKBB-internal negative codes (-600, -601, -602). Missing-data sentinels 'Prefer not to answer' (-818) and 'Not applicable' (-313, menstrual item only) are excluded from the permissible-value set per CDE convention and should be handled as missing-data qualifiers in the data model. The menstrual cramps item is administered to women only; implementers should record sex-eligibility as an administration condition for that item. A total PHQ-12 SS score can be derived by summing scored items. Near-miss NHANES CDEs address general health worry/concern over the past month and are conceptually distinct (different instrument, recall window, and symptom specificity).

records.concept: Hours per day spent driving on a typical driving day
records.idealCde: Driving frequency and duration in a typical week: captures (1) the number of days per week the respondent normally drives on average, reported as a whole number (0–7 days/week); (2) the number of hours per day spent driving on a typical driving day, reported as a non-negative numeric value (hours/day); and (3) the number of minutes per day spent driving on a typical driving day beyond whole hours, reported as a non-negative numeric value (minutes/day). Together these three components characterize habitual personal vehicle driving exposure. No specific qualifier (e.g., work vs. leisure, vehicle type) is specified in the source fields.

records.concept: Online mental health/well-being questionnaire administration date (invitation sent, module start, module completion)
records.idealCde: Online mental health/well-being questionnaire administration date: captures the calendar date associated with a participant's engagement with an online mental health or well-being questionnaire, encompassing invitation sent date, module start date, and module completion date. Question answered: 'What is the date on which the online mental health/well-being questionnaire (or a specified module thereof) was initiated, completed, or for which an invitation was dispatched?' Answer type: ISO 8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD), with a required qualifier specifying the event type (invitation sent / questionnaire started / questionnaire completed) and, where applicable, the module name (e.g., General Health, Mental Health).

gencde.title: Online Mental Health / Well-Being Questionnaire Administration Date

gencde.rationale: All six source fields from UK Biobank resolve to ISO 8601 calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD) tied to one of three event types: (1) invitation sent, (2) module started, (3) module completed. Two questionnaire modules are represented: 'General Health' and 'Mental Health'. Because the date value itself is identical in structure across all events, a single date-type CDE is appropriate; a mandatory companion qualifier variable (event_type: invitation_sent | module_started | module_completed) and an optional module qualifier (general_health | mental_health | overall) should accompany this element at the dataset level. No numeric range or permissible-value enumeration applies to a date field. Near-miss CDEs (SPMSQ date items, self-rated mental health) were excluded as they capture questionnaire content rather than administration metadata.

records.concept: Presence of sleep change (yes/no/don't know/prefer not to answer)
records.idealCde: Sleep disturbance symptom complex: a set of related items capturing (1) presence of sleep change (yes/no/don't know/prefer not to answer), (2) direction of sleep change — specifically sleeping too much (hypersomnia; yes/no), (3) severity/functional impact of difficulty sleeping on usual activities (categorical: not limiting / causing avoidance or reduction of activities / don't know / prefer not to answer), (4) functional interference of sleep-related problems with normal life roles including work/study/childcare/housework/leisure (ordinal scale from 'not at all' to severe interference, with prefer-not-to-answer option), and (5) duration of difficulty sleeping (categorical: <2 weeks / 2–4 weeks / 4–12 weeks / >12 weeks / don't know / prefer not to answer). Each item is a categorical single-select response. The overarching question answered is: 'Has the respondent experienced a change in sleep, and if so, what is the nature (too much/too little), severity of functional limitation, impact on normal roles, and duration of that sleep disturbance?' Answer type: categorical single-select per sub-item; no physical units; response options include 'do not know' and 'prefer not to answer' sentinel values throughout.

gencde.title: Presence of Sleep Change (Yes/No)
gencde.definition: A binary indicator of whether an individual has experienced any change in their sleep pattern, as self-reported in the context of a health or psychiatric symptom assessment.
gencde.questionText: Did your sleep change?
relatedCdes: Change sleep schedule difficulty PhenX
Does moving at night disrupt your sleep, wake you up at night [PhenX]
Does this loss of sleep affect you the next day with respect to...your mood (being sadder or happier)? (If yes, How?)
gencde.rationale: Source field (UKBB F20446/F20441 follow-up) included four response options: Yes, No, Do not know, and Prefer not to answer. However, the ANSWER CONCEPTS instruction restricts the canonical permissible-value set to only the concepts actually observed across harmonized cohorts: No and Yes. Sentinel/missing-data codes (-818 Prefer not to answer, -121 Do not know) are excluded per instructions. Data type is set to binary reflecting the two canonical answer concepts. This element captures only the presence/absence dimension of the broader sleep disturbance symptom complex; direction of change (hypersomnia/insomnia), severity, and functional interference are separate sibling elements. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX sleep schedule difficulty, nocturnal movement disruption, next-day mood impact) were used only to inform aliases and confirm non-match.

gencde.rationale: Three parallel binary items from UKBB (fields: Sleeping too much, Trouble falling asleep, Waking too early) are harmonized under a single CDE template with a shared 0=No/1=Yes value domain. Each item is administered conditionally upon a prior affirmative response to a general sleep-change question (UKBB F20532). The canonical permissible values (No/Yes) are the only answer concepts observed across all source fields; missing-data sentinels and don't-know codes were not present in source and are excluded per instructions. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX early-waking, tinnitus-related insomnia) informed aliases but were not matched because they differ in scope, time window, or clinical context.

gencde.rationale: Derived from a single UK Biobank Health and Wellbeing online follow-up field (Field 28688 or similar), asked conditionally when difficulty sleeping was endorsed. transforms.sourceVariable: UKBB:Impact on normal roles during worst period of depression
transforms.rationale: The SOURCE variable uses a frequency/intensity scale (Not at all, A little, Somewhat, A lot) while the TARGET CDE uses a difficulty scale (Not difficult at all, Somewhat difficult, Very difficult, Extremely difficult). Only 'Somewhat' (2) maps confidently to 'Somewhat difficult'. '0=Not at all' could conceptually map to 'Not difficult at all' but the phrasing differs enough to be uncertain. '1=A little' and '3=A lot' have no direct CDE equivalents. '-818=Prefer not to answer' is a missing-data sentinel with no CDE equivalent. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:c660d0c5d1333#g3): 5 of 5 source codes now map.

records.concept: General availability of destinations within easy walking distance of home

cde.id: Many shops, stores, markets, or other places to buy things I need are within easy walking distance of my home [PhenX]

records.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability and destination accessibility (self-reported, home context): A set of items assessing the respondent's perception of their immediate residential neighborhood's walkability, capturing three distinct sub-constructs — (1) general availability of destinations within easy walking distance of home, (2) proximity of shops/stores/markets to home within easy walking distance, and (3) proximity of a public transit stop (bus, train, trolley, or tram) within a 10–15 minute walk from home. Each item is answered on a 4-point Likert agreement scale (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree), with additional options for Don't know/Not sure and Prefer not to say. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; qualifier: self-report about the respondent's own home neighborhood environment.

records.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability and destination accessibility (self-reported, home context): A set of items assessing the respondent's perception of their immediate residential neighborhood's walkability, capturing three distinct sub-constructs — (1) general availability of destinations within easy walking distance of home, (2) proximity of shops/stores/markets to home within easy walking distance, and (3) proximity of a public transit stop (bus, train, trolley, or tram) within a 10–15 minute walk from home. Each item is answered on a 4-point Likert agreement scale (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree), with additional options for Don't know/Not sure and Prefer not to say. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; qualifier: self-report about the respondent's own home neighborhood environment.

records.concept: Digital Volume Pulse (DVP) waveform morphology decomposition measurements (notch position, peak position, shoulder position, peak-to-peak time, raw waveform data, reflection index)
records.idealCde: Digital Volume Pulse (DVP) waveform morphology measurement: captures the decomposed components of a finger photoplethysmographic (DVP) waveform, which is modeled as the sum of a direct (forward) pressure wave from the left ventricle and a reflected wave returning from the lower body via the aorta. The CDE encompasses the following sub-elements derived from the DVP waveform decomposition: (1) position of the notch on the waveform (sample index or normalized time at which the notch between direct and reflected components occurs); (2) position of the peak on the waveform (sample index or normalized time of the overall waveform peak); (3) position of the shoulder on the waveform (sample index or normalized time of the inflection/shoulder marking the onset of the reflected component); (4) peak-to-peak time between the direct and reflected component peaks (milliseconds); and (5) raw wave data comprising 3 representative DVP waveform cycles, each containing one direct and one reflected component (time-series amplitude array, arbitrary photoplethysmographic units, sampled at device-specific rate). Question answered: 'What are the morphological and temporal characteristics of the decomposed digital volume pulse waveform recorded at the finger?' Answer type: mixed — integer or floating-point sample indices or normalized positional values for waveform landmark positions; numeric continuous value in milliseconds for peak-to-peak time; time-series array of numeric amplitude values for raw waveform data.

gencde.title: Digital Volume Pulse (DVP) Waveform Morphology Decomposition Measurements
gencde.definition: A set of quantitative measurements derived from the decomposition of a finger photoplethysmographic (Digital Volume Pulse) waveform into its direct (forward) and reflected components, including the temporal positions of the notch, peak, and shoulder features, the peak-to-peak interval between direct and reflected wave peaks, the reflection index (ratio of reflected to direct wave amplitude), and the raw pressure-versus-time waveform data.
gencde.questionText: What are the morphological decomposition characteristics of the Digital Volume Pulse waveform, including the sample positions of the notch, peak, and shoulder; the peak-to-peak time between direct and reflected components; the reflection index; and the raw waveform data?

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE aggregates six closely related UKBB sub-fields that collectively describe DVP waveform morphology decomposition: (1) notch position (integer sample index), (2) peak position (integer sample index), (3) shoulder position (integer sample index), (4) peak-to-peak time (integer, ms), (5) reflection index (integer, expressed as percentage ratio of reflected-to-direct wave amplitude heights), and (6) raw waveform compound data (100-point X,Y series per beat, X in ms, Y in arbitrary pulse signal strength units). Because these sub-elements span multiple data types (integer indices, milliseconds, percentage, compound series), the parent CDE is typed as numeric with units described per sub-element. Implementers should represent each sub-element as a distinct variable linked to this parent concept. Near-miss CDEs (perfusion index, Doppler ejection time) were used only to confirm non-overlap and inform aliases. The reflection index is conceptually related to but distinct from perfusion index and augmentation index.

memberDetails.name: Position of pulse wave notch
memberDetails.text:
position of the notch

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. This is the time when when notch occurs in the waveform.
